With this on, each swipe you keep records where your finger really passed each letter, and later swipes are read against keys moved to match. It keeps a few of your own shapes for each word you swipe and leave alone, so a word you have drawn before is read against the way you draw it as well as the textbook path. And it remembers when you take a different word off the strip, or backspace a swiped word straight away, so the same stroke reads your word first next time; only scrambled fingerprints of those words are kept, never the words. Backspacing a swiped word takes its lessons back. Turn this off to freeze what has been learned, or use Forget below to start over.

title: Glide check-up
name: typing_glide_checkup_title
description: Measure your own swipes, get one change proposed with its expected effect, and confirm it later
help: Two of the numbers behind glide typing depend on what you write rather than on the keyboard: how much of the dictionary a swipe may answer with, and how much a word's commonness counts against the shape you drew. The check-up finds the right values from your own swipes. While it is measuring, each word you swipe is read again in the background under a few candidate values, and only the words that come out are kept, never the stroke. After 30 swipes it proposes one change at a time, says how many of your own swipes it would have read right, and lets you apply it. After the next 40 swipes it compares how often you corrected swiped words before and after, and offers to keep or undo. A change is never applied or undone over a value you set by hand in the meantime.

title: Space after a glided word
name: typing_space_after_glide_title
description: Add a space when you lift your finger at the end of a glide
help: This setting is on by default. The keyboard types a space after a glided word, so the next word does not join it. You can glide the next word, or type it on the keys. Type . , ? ! ; : or a closing bracket next, and the keyboard removes the space first. A press on the spacebar counts as the space that is already there. Backspace takes back the glided word and its space together. The keyboard adds no space in a password, an email address, a web address, a number pad or a phone pad.

title: Backspace removes a glided word
name: typing_glide_backspace_undo_title
description: One backspace after a glide deletes the whole word
help: This setting is on by default. Right after you glide a word, one backspace deletes the whole word and its space, and the suggestion strip shows other words for the same glide. Turn this off to delete one letter at a time, as for a word you typed on the keys. Use this when your glides are usually correct except for one or two letters.

title: Apostrophe in a glide
name: typing_glide_apostrophe_title
description: Glide through one key to put an apostrophe in the word
help: The letters have no apostrophe, so the keyboard cannot tell "its" from "it's" in a glide. Select a key here and that key means an apostrophe in a glide: swipe i, t, that key, then s, and you get "it's". The key still types its own character when you press it. Select one key only. Two keys make every word less accurate. This step is not necessary. A word you glide without it still works, and "Fix missing apostrophes" still repairs words such as "dont". The spacebar also ends a word in a glide, so "Glide across the spacebar" stops while you use the spacebar for the apostrophe.

title: Swipe start distance
name: typing_swipe_start_distance_title
description: How far to move before a glide starts. A low value is more sensitive
help: This is the finger movement that changes a press into a glide. It is a multiple of the system touch slop. A low value starts the glide sooner and is more sensitive, but a still press can start a glide. A high value needs a more deliberate swipe.

title: Delay after typing
name: typing_gesture_cooldown_title
description: Resist the start of a glide immediately after a press
help: Immediately after you press a key, a small movement off the key can look like a glide. In this window a glide must travel further before it starts, and the extra distance decreases across the window. Fast typing stays clean, and a deliberate swipe still starts. A high value stops more accidents, but a glide immediately after typing starts more slowly. 0 turns this off.

title: Start error radius
name: typing_glide_start_radius_title
description: How far the start of a glide can be from the first letter
help: Measured in key widths. The keyboard offers a word only when your finger went down this close to the first letter of that word. A high value lets a glide start off the key and still find the word. A low value refuses a glide that starts in the wrong place, which is stricter but can lose the word you wanted. Move this up if your glides start late or low.

title: End error radius
name: typing_glide_end_radius_title
description: How far the end of a glide can be from the last letter
help: Measured in key widths. The keyboard offers a word only when you lifted your finger this close to the last letter of that word. The end of a glide is where a movement stops, so it is usually less accurate than the start. This is a separate value for that reason. Move it up if your glides slide past the last letter.

title: Path error radius
name: typing_glide_near_radius_title
description: How far a glide can pass from a letter on the way
help: Measured in key widths. A letter is available to a word only when the glide passed this close to its key. A high value lets you cut corners and still get the letter. A low value keeps the keyboard to the keys you touched, which is faster and more exact, but a cut corner then loses the word. Move this up if long words come out with a letter missing.

title: Pause to mark a letter
name: typing_glide_dwell_title
description: How long to stay on a key to say the letter is in the word
help: A glide along one row of keys draws the same straight line for "write", "wire" and "wrote". Stop on a key for a moment to say that its letter is in the word, and the words without that letter lose. The stop counts for the key you stop on, not for the keys next to it. A stop does not write a letter twice: draw a loop for that. The value is a multiple of your own speed in that same glide, not a number of seconds, so it works in a quick glide and a slow one alike. A low value accepts a short stop, but a careful glide that slows down everywhere then marks keys that it only goes past. A high value asks for a clear stop.

title: Loop to double a letter
name: typing_glide_loop_title
description: Draw a small circle on a key to write the letter twice
help: This is the mark Swype taught, and it is the only mark that writes a letter twice. Glide to the letter, go around on it one time, and carry on. The circle costs the word nothing, because the keyboard takes the loop out of the distance your finger travelled. The circle belongs to the one key nearest its middle, so the keys that its edge goes over stay out of the word. Turn this off if your glides curl on the way and you get letters written twice that you did not ask for.

title: Loop sensitivity
name: typing_glide_loop_arc_title
description: How much of a circle a curl must be to count as one
help: Measured in key widths of drawn path. A low value reads a small curl as a mark, which is less work to draw but also catches the shake of a slow turn. A high value asks for a circle you drew on purpose.

title: Biggest loop that counts
name: typing_glide_loop_extent_title
description: Wider circles are a path through keys, not a mark on one
help: Measured in key widths. A mark has to be small enough to sit on one key. A word such as "murderer" goes around a ring of keys next to each other and draws a wide circle that means nothing of the sort, so keep this under the width of one key. A low value counts only a tight circle and keeps the letters around it out of it.

title: Loop centring
name: typing_glide_loop_radius_title
description: How near the letter the middle of a circle must be
help: Measured in key widths. The keyboard gives a circle to the one key nearest its middle, and only if that key is this near. A circle drawn through a key sits about a third of a key to one side, so a very low value finds no letter for it and the mark does nothing. A high value also accepts a circle drawn between two keys, and gives it to the nearer one.

title: Wiggle to mark a letter
name: typing_glide_wiggle_title
description: Rub back and forth on a key to say the letter is in the word
help: The moving way to do what a pause does: instead of a stop, scrub over the key. It says that the letter is in the word. It does not write the letter twice. This is off, because a slow turn drawn with an unsteady finger looks much the same, and the keyboard then marks keys that you only went past. Turn it on if this is the mark you make.

title: Wiggle strength
name: typing_glide_wiggle_strength_title
description: How much a rub counts, compared with a full stop
help: A value of 100 percent makes a rub as strong as a full stop on the key. A lower value leaves it as a hint, which a much more common word can still win against. Used only while the switch above is on.

title: Biggest wiggle that counts
name: typing_glide_wiggle_extent_title
description: How far the finger can go in a rub
help: Measured in key widths. Keep this under the width of one key, or a word that goes from one key to the key next door and back reads as a rub on one key. Used only while the switch above is on.

title: Shapes kept per word
name: typing_glide_shapes_per_word_title
description: How many ways of swiping one word are remembered
help: Learn my swipe style keeps your own shapes for each word you swipe, and a swipe is read against the nearest of them. Swipe a word the same way and the shape settles in; swipe it a clearly different way and that is kept as another shape, up to this many, the least used making room. Raise it if you swipe some words several different ways and the keyboard keeps forgetting one of them. The shapes travel in a backup under Swipe style, so you can see how many your words really use. Lowering it takes the extras out of use at once, and they are only deleted when that word next learns a new shape. Used only while Learn my swipe style is on.

title: Trail style
name: typing_trail_style_title
description: The line a glide draws behind your finger
help: A glide draws a line behind your finger so you can see the stroke. Thin, Normal and Bold set its width, how long it lingers and how solid it is together. Off draws no line at all, and the glide still types. The three sliders under More settings set each of those on its own.

title: Trail width
name: typing_trail_width_title
description: Thickness of the glide trail

title: Trail length
name: typing_trail_length_title
description: How long the trail stays behind your finger

title: Word preview
name: typing_glide_preview_title
description: Float the word above your finger as you glide
help:
While you glide, the word that the keyboard reads so far floats above your finger, and it changes as you go. Turn this off and the word appears only on the suggestion strip.

This does not change what a glide types.

title: Preview distance above finger
name: typing_glide_preview_height_title
description: How far above your finger the word floats
help:
Your hand covers more of the screen than your fingertip does, so the word can end up behind it. Raise this until you can read the word while you glide.

The word is drawn inside the keyboard. Near the top row, a large distance stops at the top edge.

title: Preview sideways shift
name: typing_glide_preview_shift_title
description: Move the word left or right of your finger
help:
Your hand covers one side of your finger more than the other. Move the word to the other side and you can read it without moving your hand.

A negative value moves it to the left. A positive value moves it to the right. Near the edge of the keyboard the word stops at the edge.

title: Preview text size
name: typing_glide_preview_size_title
description: Size of the word that floats above your finger
help: This is the size of the text in the floating word only. The suggestion strip and the keys do not change.

title: Preview color
name: typing_glide_preview_color_title
description: Background behind the floating word
help: By default the floating word takes its color from the keyboard theme, which is the same color as the key popup. Pick a color here and it uses that instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

title: Preview text color
name: typing_glide_preview_text_color_title
description: Color of the floating word itself
help: By default the floating word takes its text color from the keyboard theme. Pick a color here and it uses that instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

title: One word on the strip
name: typing_glide_strip_preview_title
description: While you glide, show only the current word
help:
While you glide, the suggestion strip shows every word that fits your stroke, and the words change as you move. Turn this on and the strip shows only the word that the keyboard reads now.

The other words come back on the strip when you lift your finger. If the ambiguity picker is on, it still offers them during the stroke. This does not change what a glide types.

title: Measure my swipes
name: typing_glide_checkup_measure_title
description: Read each swiped word again under a few candidate values, in the background
help: On, each word you swipe costs a few more decodes after it is typed, off the keyboard's thread. Only the words that come out are kept, up to 200 of them; no stroke is stored. Turn it off once you have a change you are happy with.

title: Quick swipe on the spacebar
name: typing_space_short_swipe_title
description: A swipe that starts to move immediately
help: Swipe left or right on the spacebar without a pause. "Language" steps through your input modes, with a live preview above the spacebar. Lift your finger to switch. Press and hold the spacebar to show the picker before you swipe. That only works while "Press and hold, then swipe" is set to the language or to nothing, because that setting owns the hold. "Cursor" moves the text cursor one character for each step. A press without movement always types a space.

title: Press and hold, then swipe
name: typing_space_long_swipe_title
description: Press and hold the spacebar, then swipe
help: Press and hold the spacebar past the hold delay, then swipe. This gives the spacebar a second, separate swipe action. Example: a quick swipe switches the language, and a press and hold with a swipe moves the cursor. You can also set both to the same action. Anything but the language here takes the hold for itself, so holding the spacebar stops opening the language picker. The picker stays on the globe key and on the quick swipe.

title: Swipe up for the touchpad
name: typing_space_swipe_up_touchpad_title
description: A swipe up from the spacebar moves the cursor in every direction
help: Swipe up from the spacebar, then keep your finger down and move it: the cursor follows left, right, up and down, like the 2-D cursor touchpad, until you lift. The swipe has to go a short way up first, so a tap that slides a little still types a space. Sideways swipes keep the actions set above, so a quick swipe can still switch the language and you do not have to hold the spacebar first. With Keep moving while held and Whole keyboard as touchpad both on, the cursor keeps going when your finger reaches any edge of the keyboard: the sides move it along the line, the top and bottom move it between lines. This setting is off by default.

title: Swipe up for the number pad
name: typing_space_swipe_up_numpad_title
description: A swipe up from the spacebar opens the number pad
help: Swipe up from the spacebar, at any speed, and the number pad opens, the way SwiftKey does it. The swipe has to go a short way up first, so a tap that slides a little still types a space. Sideways swipes keep the actions set above. If Swipe up for the touchpad is on as well, the touchpad wins. This setting is off by default.

title: 2-D cursor touchpad
name: typing_space_cursor_2d_title
description: The cursor swipe also moves up and down
help: This setting changes the spacebar cursor swipe into a touchpad. The cursor moves left and right, and a swipe up or down moves the cursor between lines. This applies only to the swipe actions set to "Cursor" above.

title: Cursor speed
name: typing_space_cursor_step_title
description: How far you slide along the spacebar to move one character
help: A smaller distance moves the cursor faster, so a short spacebar can still cross a long line. A larger one is steadier if your slides tend to overshoot. This setting is 16 dp by default.

title: Speed up long cursor swipes
name: typing_space_cursor_accelerate_title
description: The further a spacebar swipe goes, the faster the cursor moves
help: After a short distance at the normal cursor speed, each character needs less movement. The speed increases until it gets to the top speed, and it stays at that speed while you continue in the same direction. When you go back, the speed starts again at the normal speed, so you can correct an overshoot accurately. With the 2-D cursor touchpad, movement up and down also increases speed in the same way. A short swipe moves one character at a time, as before. This setting is off by default.

title: Move the cursor directly
name: typing_space_cursor_direct_title
description: Place the cursor instead of pressing arrow keys
help: A spacebar swipe normally moves the cursor by pressing the left and right arrow keys, the way a hardware keyboard would. Some search boxes read an arrow key as a step through their suggestions, and some file managers put the cursor back at the start of the name after one. With this setting on, the swipe places the cursor directly instead, and no app sees a key press. The app has to tell the keyboard where its cursor is for this to work; when it does not, the arrow keys are used as before. With the 2-D cursor touchpad on, up and down in a one-line field, such as a search box, put the cursor at the start or the end of the text instead of pressing the up and down arrows. In a field with several lines they stay arrow keys, so the cursor follows the app's own line wrapping. Selection mode and a held shift stretch the selection the same way, by setting it rather than pressing Shift and an arrow. This setting is off by default.

title: Keep moving while held
name: typing_space_cursor_edge_repeat_title
description: A cursor swipe held still, or past the end of the spacebar, keeps going
help: The spacebar is shorter than a long line of text. With this setting on, a cursor swipe keeps going by itself, about eight characters a second: at once when your finger is past either end of the spacebar, and after a short pause when you hold your finger still away from where the swipe began. Move your finger again, or lift it, to stop. Short swipes and fine adjustments near where you started are not affected. This setting is off by default.

title: Whole keyboard as touchpad
name: typing_space_cursor_whole_keyboard_title
description: A cursor swipe can use the whole keyboard, and the other keys pause
help: Once a spacebar swipe starts moving the cursor, the whole keyboard becomes its touchpad. The keys dim, and touching them with another finger types nothing until you lift. With Keep moving while held on, the cursor keeps going when your finger reaches either side of the keyboard rather than the end of the spacebar. Your finger can always leave the spacebar during a swipe; this setting stops the other keys from reacting while it does. This setting is off by default.

title: Top cursor speed
name: typing_space_cursor_top_speed_title
description: How fast a long spacebar swipe moves the cursor at its fastest
help: The value is how many times faster than the normal cursor speed the cursor goes at the end of a long swipe. This setting is 4× by default.

title: Cursor magnifier
name: typing_space_cursor_magnifier_title
description: Show the text at the cursor, larger, while a spacebar swipe moves the cursor
help: The magnifier shows the line of text around the cursor. It goes above the cursor when the app tells the keyboard where the cursor is. If the app does not, it goes above the keyboard. The trackpad tool has a separate setting for this.

title: Swipe down to hide the keyboard
name: typing_space_swipe_down_hide_title
description: A swipe down on the spacebar closes the keyboard
help: Swipe straight down on the spacebar to close the keyboard. This setting is off by default, so an accidental swipe down never closes the keyboard. When the 2-D cursor touchpad is on, a swipe down moves the cursor instead. The touchpad has priority.

title: Arrows on the spacebar
name: typing_spacebar_language_arrows_title
description: Show that a swipe switches the language
help: The keyboard draws a small ◀ and ▶ on each side of the language name on the spacebar. They are only a hint, and the swipe works without them. They stay hidden while one input mode only is on.

title: Keep the new language on screen
name: typing_language_echo_title
description: How long a spacebar swipe shows the language it switched to
help: A quick flick on the spacebar is over before its preview can draw, so the keyboard keeps the language it landed on up for a moment after you lift, to show where you went. This is how long it stays, counting the time the preview was already up. Slide to Off to have it go the instant you lift. A slow swipe that rested on its language for a quarter of a second has already shown it, so it goes at once whatever this is set to.

title: Language picker shape
name: typing_language_picker_style_title
description: A list to drag through, or a carousel that keeps the swipe sideways
help: This is the chooser that opens when you hold the spacebar with more than four layouts on, or press and hold the 🌐 key. List shows your layouts top to bottom, and a hold on the spacebar walks it up and down. Carousel shows them side by side, centred on the one you are typing in, and the same hold walks it left and right, the way the spacebar swipe already moves. Both let you tap a layout, and both keep Other keyboards… at the end.

title: Picker for more than four layouts
name: typing_space_hold_picker_long_ring_title
description: Hold the spacebar to open the picker when more than four layouts are on
help: With four layouts or fewer, holding the spacebar shows the sideways preview above it, and a drag steps through your layouts. Past four, the hold opens the picker instead, as a list or a carousel. Turn this off to keep the sideways preview however many layouts are on. It shows five at a time and slides along as you drag, so every layout is still in reach. The 🌐 key's long press still opens the picker. If the quick swipe is not set to Language, the hold opens the picker at any length.

title: The spacebar shows
name: typing_spacebar_display_title
description: What the spacebar label shows at rest
help: Language shows the name of the current language. Layout shows the name of the current layout. Both shows "Language (Layout)". Nothing leaves the spacebar blank, apart from your own text below; the language picker still shows names. When one language has more than one layout on, the keyboard adds the layout name, so you can see the difference.

title: Typing speed on the spacebar
name: typing_spacebar_live_wpm_title
description: Show your words per minute while you type
help: The spacebar shows how fast you typed your last few words, next to its label. The number changes each time a word goes in, and typed, picked, glided and two-thumb words all count. After a pause of 5 seconds the spacebar shows only its label again. The keyboard keeps no record of this number. It works when Statistics is off and in incognito mode.

title: Swipe down to type the hint
name: typing_hint_flick_title
description: A quick swipe down on a key types its small corner character
help: Each key shows its first press-and-hold character in the corner, such as 1 on q. A short, quick swipe straight down on the key types that character with no hold. This works on any key that has press-and-hold characters, on every layer. The spacebar, backspace and the shift and modifier keys keep their own swipes. The swipe must be short, straight down and fast. A longer or slower drag is a glide, as before. A swipe that ends on another letter, such as "ok" from o to k, is a glided word, not a flick. This setting is off by default.

title: Swipe up for a capital
name: typing_capital_flick_title
description: A quick swipe up on a letter types it as a capital
help: A short, quick swipe straight up on a letter types its capital, with no need to press shift first. On a key that has its own shifted character, such as a number key with a symbol above it, the swipe types that character. The swipe must be short, straight up and fast, like the swipe down for the hint. A longer or slower drag is a glide, as before. If Words on the keys shows a word on the key, a swipe up still takes that word. A swipe that ends on another letter, such as "de" from d to e, is a glided word, not a flick. This setting is off by default.

title: Show flick arms on keys
name: typing_flick_hints_title
description: A key with flick characters shows them small at its edges and corners
help: Some keys type a different character when you swipe from them in one of eight directions: the Japanese flick pad, the English flick (3×3) layout, and any key you give flick directions in the layout editor. With this on, each key draws its flick characters small, at the edge or corner you swipe towards, so you can see what a swipe types before you make it. The centre character stays large. Turn it off to show only the centre character, as the kana pad did before. On by default.

title: Flick popup
name: typing_flick_popup_title
description: Holding a flick key shows its characters in a cross, with the one under your finger lit
help: While you hold a key that has flick directions, a popup over the key shows the centre character and all its flick characters in a 3×3 grid. The one your finger is moving towards is lit, so you can check before you lift. Turn this off if the keys already show their flick arms and you do not want a popup covering the keys around them. On by default.

title: Tap a swipe-only key to see its swipes
name: typing_swipe_only_tap_title
description: A key with flick characters and no centre shows them for a moment when tapped
help: A key can have flick characters and nothing in the middle: leave its label empty in the layout editor, or import an Unexpected Keyboard layout with keys like that. Only the swipes type anything. Off, the default, a tap on such a key does nothing. On, the tap brings up the key's flick popup for a moment so you can see what each swipe types, even if Flick popup is turned off.

title: Flick distance
name: typing_flick_distance_title
description: How far your finger moves before a press on a flick key becomes a flick
help: A press on a flick key is a tap until your finger has moved this far. Lower the distance for a quick, short flick on a small key. Raise it if a tap that drifts a little flicks when you did not mean it to. The default is 22 dp, which the Japanese flick pad has always used. A swipe out to a flick character and more than halfway back again types that character's capital.

title: Flick reach
name: typing_flick_reach_title
description: How far a swipe from a flick key can go and still be a flick, before glide typing takes it
help: With glide typing on, a swipe that starts on a letter with flick characters stays a flick until it travels this far from where your finger landed, measured against the key's diagonal. Past that, the swipe is a glided word. A swipe that turns, or that reaches another letter in a direction no flick character points, becomes a word sooner. Lower the reach if long glides from those keys start late; raise it if a long flick turns into a word. The default is 141%.

title: A flick onto a letter glides a word
name: typing_flick_onto_letter_title
description: A short swipe that ends on the next letter types a word, even where a flick character points that way
help: With glide typing on, a short straight swipe from one letter onto its neighbour can mean two things when the first key has a flick character pointing that way: the flick character, or a two-letter word. Off, the default, the flick character wins, so a flick that overshoots still types what it points at. On, lifting inside another letter types the word instead, and a flick has to stop short of the next key. A swipe in a direction with no flick character is a word either way.

title: Swipe to add 's
name: typing_possessive_swipe_title
description: Swipe from a punctuation key to s to add 's to the last word, or to t, d, m, l, r or v for 't, 'd, 'm, 'll, 're or 've
help: Select a key here. A short, straight swipe from that key to the s key adds 's to the word before the cursor, so "developer" becomes "developer's". Swipe to t, d, m, l, r or v to add 't, 'd, 'm, 'll, 're or 've. 't is added only after a word that ends in n, so "don" becomes "don't". A line from the key to your finger shows that the swipe is active. This works after you type a word and after you glide one, with glide typing on or off. A space after the word moves behind the 's. The key still types its own character when you press it. The swipe must be short and straight. A longer path from the same key to s is a glide, as before. This works with English only. The spacebar cannot start this swipe.

title: Swipe in from the edge to go back
name: typing_edge_swipe_back_title
description: A swipe in from the left or right edge of the keyboard closes a panel or the keyboard
help: Some phones do not let the back gesture of the system start over the keyboard, so you must start it above the keyboard. With this setting on, a swipe that starts at the left or right edge of the keyboard and moves in does the same thing. It closes the panel that is open, for example the voice panel, which also stops the recording. When no panel is open, it closes the keyboard. This setting is off by default, because a glide that starts at the very edge and moves in looks the same. Start glides a little in from the edge.

title: Multi-finger swipes
name: typing_finger_swipes_title
description: Swipe two, three or four fingers together over the keys to run an action
help: Put two or more fingers on the keys and swipe them the same way together. Instead of typing, the swipe runs the action you chose for that number of fingers and that direction. Out of the box, two fingers up selects all the text, left undoes, right redoes and down pastes. Three and four fingers start empty. Fast typing is not mistaken for a swipe: every finger has to travel the same way before anything happens, and lifting one first leaves the keys to type as usual. A line follows each finger while the swipe is on.

title: Reset swipe actions
name: typing_finger_swipes_reset_title
description: Put every multi-finger swipe back to its default

title: Chords with ?123
name: typing_symbol_chords_title
description: Hold ?123 still and tap a key to run an action
help: Hold ?123 still with one finger and tap a key with another. Instead of typing that key, the keyboard runs the action you chose for it, and letting go of ?123 leaves you on the letters. Out of the box, ?123 and L switches to your next language. Hold ?123 a moment and each key with a chord shows it on its face. A key with no chord types as usual, and a drag off ?123 still shows the symbols. The chord needs ?123 held first: rolling off ?123 straight onto the next key is too quick to count. It works with two-thumb typing, where a held key never becomes part of a swipe.

title: Add a chord
name: typing_symbol_chord_add_title
description: Pick a key, then what it does

title: Reset chords
name: typing_symbol_chords_reset_title
description: Put the chords back to the default

title: Swipes on keys
name: typing_key_swipes_title
description: Your own short swipes off letter keys, on every layout
help: Put a character or an action on any of the eight directions around a key, and a short swipe that way off the key types it or runs it. The swipes belong to the key, not to a layout, so the 1 you put up and to the right of Q is there on QWERTY, AZERTY and every other layout with a Q. Where a layout already has a swipe in that direction, the layout's own swipe stays. Each key draws its swipes small on its face, and glide typing still works: a swipe that turns, or carries on into another letter, glides a word. A key with swipes gives up the swipe down for its hint and the slide to select. Only the letters page gets them.

title: Add a key
name: typing_key_swipe_add_title
description: Pick a key, then what each swipe off it does

title: Add a preset
name: typing_key_swipe_preset_title
description: Numbers, symbols or editing shortcuts in one go

title: Remove all key swipes
name: typing_key_swipes_reset_title
description: Take every swipe you added off the keys

title: Process the physical keys
name: typing_hardware_input_title
description: Transliterate, correct and suggest as you type on a physical keyboard
help:
With a physical keyboard connected, the keys go through the same engine as the on-screen keyboard. Phonetic layouts transliterate, so "ami" gives "আমি". Words compose for suggestions, and autocorrect runs when you press space. The word you type shows with an underline in the field until you finish it.

Shortcuts (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Z), the arrow keys, the function keys and everything in password fields always go straight to the app, at any setting.

Turn this off to type the raw characters straight into the field. The layout of the physical keyboard then controls the input.

title: Tool shortcuts
name: typing_hw_shortcuts_title
description: Open tools from a physical keyboard without touching the screen
help:
Press the shortcut key. Each button on the keyboard then shows the key that operates it: a number under each toolbar icon, a letter under each tool in the toolbox, and Shift with a key for the symbol and emoji rows.

T opens the full toolbox, and ? shows the list of every key, including the tools that are not on the screen.

The shortcut key is two presses of Ctrl by default. No app uses this, because a Ctrl alone makes no character, and the keyboard still passes it through. You can change the shortcut key and every letter below.

title: Arrow keys move a highlight
name: typing_hw_panel_nav_title
description: Arrows move a highlight in a tool, Enter selects it, Esc closes the tool
help:
In a tool, the arrow keys move a highlight over the emoji, the clips or the results. Enter uses the item with the highlight. Tab moves between the search box, the category chips and the results.

The highlight shows only after you press a key. It never shows while you use the keyboard by touch.

title: Arrow keys move over the keys
name: typing_hw_dpad_keys_title
description: A ring on one key; the centre button or Enter types it
help:
For a television remote, which has no other way to reach a key. The arrow keys move a ring from key to key and the centre button types the key it is on. Left and right stay inside the row. Up from the top row leaves the keyboard, so the remote can go back to the app.

Hold the centre button to open the alternates of the key the ring is on, then pick one with the arrows. Escape puts the ring away, so Enter goes back to the text field.

On a television this is on to begin with. Everywhere else it starts off, because the arrow keys belong to the text field you are typing in.

title: Esc closes the tool
name: typing_hw_esc_title
description: Escape closes an open tool instead of going to the app
help: Escape closes only what the keyboard has open. With no tool open, Escape goes straight to the app, so it still stops a page load or exits insert mode in an editor.

title: Ctrl + number opens a toolbar tool
name: typing_hw_digit_chord_title
description: Ctrl+1 opens the toolbox, Ctrl+2 the first tool, and so on
help:
The numbers count the buttons on the toolbar from the start. Ctrl+1 is the toolbox button, Ctrl+2 is the first tool after it. Ctrl+0 is the tenth button.

This needs no shortcut key first. Turn it off if you use Ctrl with a number in your apps: browsers and editors change tab with it, and the keyboard takes the key first while you write in a text field.

The same numbers also work after the shortcut key, at any setting.

title: Ctrl+Space changes the language
name: typing_hw_lang_chord_title
description: Hold Ctrl to browse the language list, release to switch
help:
Ctrl+Space goes to the next language and Ctrl+Shift+Space to the one before. Keep Ctrl held and press Space again to step through the list on screen. The keyboard switches when Ctrl comes back up. Esc cancels.

Some apps use Ctrl+Space themselves, for example code editors use it to show completions. While this is on, the keyboard takes the shortcut when you type in those apps. Turn it off here to give it back.

If the shortcut key that opens tools is also set to Ctrl+Space, the language switch wins. A keyboard with its own language key does not need this setting: that key always works.

title: Write the modifier names
name: typing_hw_modifier_words_title
description: Show Ctrl and Shift on the keys instead of their symbols
help:
The keys under each button read "Ctrl+2" and "Shift+Q". These are the names printed on a PC keyboard.

Turn this off for the shorter symbols. They take less space, but they come from Mac keyboards, and a keyboard that does not print them gives you no help to read them.

title: Time to press a key
name: typing_hw_picker_timeout_title
description: How long the keys stay on the screen after the shortcut key
help:
After you press the shortcut key, each button shows the key that operates it. This is how long they stay before the keyboard goes back to usual.

Make this longer while you learn the keys. Make it shorter when you know them, because the keyboard does nothing else until the time is finished or you press a key.

title: Number keys select suggestions
name: typing_hw_suggestion_hotkeys_title
description: Type a suggestion by its number in the suggestion strip
help:
You cannot press the suggestion strip while you type on a physical keyboard. A number key selects a suggestion instead.

"After the shortcut key" is the safe choice, because nothing else uses it. "Alt + number" needs one key less, but browsers, editors and chat apps use a modifier with a number to switch tabs and workspaces.

For no extra key at all, set a pick mode key below. While pick mode is on, the number keys select suggestions on their own, Shift with a number types the number, and Shift+Alt with a number types the symbol on that key.

title: Show the suggestion numbers
name: typing_hw_suggestion_hints_title
description: Put the key under each suggestion while a physical keyboard is connected
help:
Each suggestion shows the key that selects it, for as long as a physical keyboard is connected.

This applies only to "Alt + number", which needs no shortcut key first. With "After the shortcut key", the numbers show after you press the shortcut key, because that is when they operate.

title: Pick mode key
name: typing_hw_pick_mode_key_title
description: A key that makes the number keys select suggestions until you press it again

title: F-keys press the toolbar
name: typing_hw_function_keys_title
description: F1 opens all tools and F2 to F10 press the toolbar buttons
help:
F1 to F10 work like Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+0: F1 opens all tools, and F2 presses the first button on the toolbar. While this works, the toolbar shows F1, F2 and so on under its buttons when you press the shortcut key.

"In pick mode" leaves the F-keys to the app until you turn pick mode on. "Always" takes them all the time, which gets in the way of terminals and code editors that use them.

title: macOS shortcuts
name: typing_hw_mac_title
description: Command and Option behave as they do on a Mac
help:
For a keyboard made for a Mac. Command is the key next to the space bar.

Command+C, Command+V, Command+X and Command+A copy, paste, cut and select all. Command+Z is undo and Command+Shift+Z is redo. Command+Left and Command+Right go to the start and the end of the line. Option+Left and Option+Right move one word. Option+Backspace deletes one word, and Command+Backspace deletes to the start of the line. Hold Shift with a move to select.

Ctrl keeps its usual behaviour, and every other Command shortcut goes to the app. Some devices keep a small number of Command shortcuts for the system, and those do not reach the keyboard.

title: Show the keyboard for shortcuts
name: typing_hw_auto_show_title
description: A shortcut that opens a tool also shows the keyboard
help: With a physical keyboard, there is usually no on-screen keyboard, and a tool has no space to draw. With this setting on, a shortcut that opens a tool shows the keyboard. When you close the tool, the keyboard hides again.

title: Swipe to delete
name: typing_backspace_swipe_title
description: Swipe sideways on backspace to delete more than one press
help: Press backspace and swipe left. Each step of the swipe deletes one more word, or one more character, as you set below. A plain press, or a press and hold, still deletes one character at a time.

title: Swipe deletes
name: typing_backspace_unit_title
description: What one step of the backspace swipe takes off
help: Words clear a sentence in one pull. Characters walk back a letter at a time, which is the finer tool when you must fix the middle of a word. The distance for one step is set below, and it is a different distance for each of the two.

title: Show what you will delete
name: typing_backspace_preview_title
description: Select the text as you swipe, and delete it when you lift your finger
help: The swipe highlights the text it is about to delete instead of deleting as it goes, so you can see how far you have got. Swipe back to the right to give text back, and lift your finger to delete what is left highlighted. Turn this off to delete each word or character the moment you swipe past it.

title: Word delete distance
name: typing_backspace_step_title
description: How far you swipe backspace to delete the first word
help: Later words come off faster than the first on a fixed curve, so this one distance tunes the whole gesture. Raise it if words disappear by accident, lower it if clearing a sentence takes too long a pull. This setting is 72 dp by default.

title: Character delete distance
name: typing_backspace_char_step_title
description: How far you swipe backspace for each character
help: Every character costs the same pull, with no speed up, so the count stays easy to follow. Raise it if letters go by too quickly, lower it if a long correction takes too much room. This setting is 20 dp by default.

title: Swipe on forward delete
name: typing_forward_delete_swipe_title
description: Swipe right on the forward delete key to clear the text ahead
help:
Press the forward delete key and swipe right. Each step of the swipe deletes one more word, or one more character, ahead of the cursor. It is the backspace swipe pointed the other way, and it follows the same three settings above: what one step takes off, whether you see it first, and how far you drag for one step.

The forward delete key is not on the standard keyboard. Add it to a row, or to a key you press and hold, in the layout editor.

title: Backspace as a key press on web pages
name: typing_web_backspace_key_title
description: Lets code editors and other page editors see backspace
help: In a text box on a web page, or in an app that shows one, backspace is sent the way a physical keyboard sends it. Some page editors, like the code editor in Violentmonkey, only delete when they see that key press. Other keyboards delete the text directly, and these editors put it back. The browser then decides how much one press deletes. If you set your language to delete a whole conjunct at once, backspace keeps deleting directly. Turn this off if backspace does something unexpected on a website.

title: Alternate key size
name: keypress_alternates_size_title
description: Text size in the press and hold popup
help:
This multiplies the size of the characters in the popup that opens when you press and hold a key. It reaches further than the popup font size above, because the popup of alternates grows to fit whatever you put in it.

The preview bubble keeps its own size, so a large value here does not push the character out of the bubble.

title: Alternate key spacing
name: keypress_alternates_padding_title
description: Room around each character in the popup
help:
This is the space around each alternate. It sets the gap between them and the size of the area that you can tap, so raise it if you hit the wrong character.

A higher value makes the popup wider, and a wide popup wraps onto more rows.

title: Alternate key columns
name: keypress_alternates_columns_title
description: How many alternates go on one row
help:
Auto puts as many alternates on a row as fit on the screen, so the shape of the popup follows the width of the characters.

A number from 3 to 11 gives every row that many columns of the same width. A key with many alternates then reads as a block, and each alternate is in the same place each time that you open it.

title: Closest to the key first
name: keypress_alternates_nearest_title
description: Fill the popup from the key outward
help:
The popup opens above the key that you hold. This decides which end of it the first alternate goes to.

Off: the first alternate is at the top left and the popup fills downward, like lines of text. On a popup of several rows, the first alternate is then the furthest from your finger.

On: the first alternate is on the row nearest the key, and the rest climb away from it. This is what most stock keyboards do, and it is a shorter reach on a key with many alternates. A popup of one row looks the same either way.

title: Centre on the key
name: keypress_alternates_centred_title
description: Put the other alternates on both sides of the first
help:
The first alternate always opens right over the key that you hold.

On: the others go on both sides of it, one to the right, one to the left, and so on outward, so a slide either way reaches the next one. A key near the edge of the screen has no room on one side, so its popup runs away from the edge instead.

Off: the others follow the first in reading order, all to one side of it.

title: Order of the alternates
name: keypress_alternates_order_title
description: Which group comes first in a letter's popup
help: A letter's popup can hold three kinds of character: the alternates the layout itself puts under the key, the accents added by All accents and Native letters first, and the capital or shifted form added by Shifted letter on press and hold. Drag the groups into the order you want. Inside each group the order stays as it was. The first entry is the one a hold and release types, so the group you reach for most belongs at the top. The default is the layout's own, then the accents, then the capital.

title: Press and hold delay
name: keypress_long_press_delay_title
description: How long you hold a key before the alternate characters appear
help: This is how long you hold a key before its alternate characters appear. The alternates are accents, digits and symbols. A lower value is faster, but the popup opens by accident more easily.

title: Delete repeat interval
name: keypress_delete_repeat_title
description: How fast delete repeats while you hold it
help: While you hold delete, it repeats at this interval. Lower values delete faster.

title: Holding delete clears words
name: keypress_hold_words_title
description: A held delete key takes whole words, not letters
help:
Hold delete and, once it starts to repeat, it takes one whole word at a time instead of one letter. A single press still deletes one letter, so nothing you do quickly changes.

This works on the forward delete key as well. Each key clears the way it points: backspace takes the words before the cursor, and forward delete takes the words after it.

Word clearing has its own speed, below, because it is much faster than letter clearing.

title: Words stop at punctuation
name: keypress_word_stops_punctuation_title
description: A word delete stops at a dot, a slash or another mark
help:
This is for each delete that takes whole words: the held delete key, and the backspace swipe when it takes words.

On, "wmkeyboard.pages.dev" goes in steps: "dev", then ".", then "pages". Off, all of it goes in one step, up to the last space.

title: Words stop at capitals
name: keypress_word_stops_capitals_title
description: "GrapheneOS" goes as "OS", then "Graphene"

title: Words stop at numbers
name: keypress_word_stops_digits_title
description: "word1" goes as "1", then "word"

title: Word delete interval
name: keypress_word_delete_repeat_title
description: How fast a held delete key clears words
help: While you hold delete and it clears words, it takes one word at this interval. It is slower than the letter interval above on purpose, because one word is a much bigger step. Lower values clear faster.

title: Space repeat interval
name: keypress_space_repeat_title
description: How fast space repeats while you hold it
help: While you hold the space bar, it repeats at this interval. Space has its own value because a run of spaces is harder to correct than a run of deletes. Use a higher value here to make it slower.

title: Repeating key interval
name: keypress_custom_repeat_title
description: How fast a key you set to repeat fires while you hold it
help: This is the speed of the keys you turned Repeat while held on for in the key layout editor, such as a row of arrow keys. Delete and space keep their own speeds above. Lower values repeat faster.

title: Hold a flick to repeat it
name: keypress_flicks_repeat_title
description: A letter flicked out and held there types again and again until you lift, at the repeating key interval

title: Caps lock double press
name: keypress_caps_lock_title
description: How fast a second press of shift turns on caps lock
help: Two presses of shift inside this time turn on caps lock. A shorter time makes caps lock faster, but it starts by accident more easily. A longer time accepts a slower double press. The default is 350 ms.

title: Key sound
name: hardware_sound_key_title
description: Play a sound on every key press

title: Sound volume
name: hardware_sound_volume_title
description: Relative to the media volume of your device

title: Key press haptics
name: keypress_haptics_title
description: Vibrate on each key press
help: A short vibration confirms each key press. This includes each step of the cursor movement on the spacebar. You can change the style and the strength below.

title: Haptic strength
name: keypress_haptic_strength_title
description: Vibration length for each key press
help: This is the length of the vibration pulse in milliseconds. Longer pulses feel stronger on most devices.

title: Haptic intensity
name: keypress_haptic_intensity_title
description: Vibration amplitude for each key press
help:
This sets how hard the keyboard drives the vibration motor, from 1 to 255.

For Sharp it scales the hardware click primitive. The length stays fixed and only the strength changes.

For Custom it works only on devices whose vibration motor supports amplitude control. On other devices only the duration above has an effect.

The system "Touch feedback" vibration setting also scales the final strength.

title: Press and hold haptics
name: keypress_long_press_haptics_title
description: Vibrate when a press and hold starts
help:
The keyboard vibrates a second time when a press and hold starts. This happens when the popup of alternate characters opens, or when a press and hold action runs. It tells your finger that it can lift.

Delete and space do not change. Their key repeat already vibrates on each repeat.

title: Press and hold release haptics
name: keypress_long_press_release_title
description: Vibrate on release after a press and hold
help: The keyboard vibrates again when you lift your finger at the end of a press and hold. This completes the press, hold and release loop. It is off by default. Some users find a third vibration too much.

title: Cursor movement haptics
name: keypress_cursor_haptics_title
description: Vibrate for each step when you move the cursor with the spacebar
help: The keyboard vibrates one time for each character that the cursor moves when you slide on the spacebar or use the volume keys. Turn this off to move the cursor without vibration. The keys continue to vibrate when you press them.

title: Vibrate on space
name: keypress_vibrate_space_title
description: Vibrate when you press the spacebar
help: Turn this off to stop the vibration of the spacebar only. Every other key continues to vibrate. This helps if the long spacebar feels heavy under your thumb. The key press sound still plays if it is on. This setting is on by default.

title: Vibrate on delete swipe
name: keypress_vibrate_delete_swipe_title
description: Vibrate for each word that a backspace swipe deletes
help: When you swipe left on the backspace key, the keyboard deletes word by word and vibrates for each word. Turn this off to delete a sentence with one smooth pull and no vibration. A plain press on backspace does not change. This setting is on by default.

title: Vibrate on key repeat
name: keypress_vibrate_repeat_title
description: Vibrate on each repeat while you hold a key
help: When you hold backspace or space, the key repeats. By default each repeat vibrates. Turn this off to vibrate on the first press only. The repeats still click if "Click on key repeat" is on. This setting is on by default.

title: Vibrate past the system touch feedback switch
name: keypress_haptics_hardware_title
description: Keep the Custom, Sharp and Click styles working when Android's touch feedback is off
help: Android silences ordinary short vibrations when you turn off touch feedback in its sound settings. The System styles have always got past that, but the Custom, Sharp, Click and Heavy click styles went quiet with it. With this on, those styles vibrate as hardware feedback, which that switch does not silence. They still follow Android's vibration strength setting. Turn this off if the vibration feels wrong on your phone. Needs Android 13 or newer. This setting is on by default.

title: Mute haptics in Do Not Disturb
name: keypress_dnd_mute_title
description: Stop all keyboard vibration while Do Not Disturb is on
help: By default the keyboard continues to vibrate in Do Not Disturb. Do Not Disturb applies to notifications, not to touch feedback. Turn this on to make the keyboard fully silent while Do Not Disturb is on. This setting is off by default.

title: Key popup
name: keypress_popup_title
description: Show a character bubble above the pressed key
help: While you hold a key, its character floats in a bubble above your finger. This lets you see the key that you pressed.

title: Popup on number pads
name: keypress_popup_numeric_title
description: Also show the bubble on number, phone, and date fields
help:
Number, phone, and date and time fields use a keypad. The floating character adds little there. Over a PIN it shows each digit large enough for another person to read it.

Turn this off to hide the bubble on those keypads. Normal text fields do not change.

title: Space above the keyboard
name: keypress_popup_window_band_title
description: Keep a clear band above the top row for its bubbles
help:
The keyboard keeps a clear band above its top row, so the bubble of a top-row key shows in full over the app. Apps still fill the screen down to the keys.

Some phones move an app in a floating window clear of that band as well, and squash the window against the top of the screen. Turn this off if that happens. The bubble of a top-row key then stays inside the keyboard, over the key itself.

title: Minimum popup duration
name: keypress_popup_min_duration_title
description: How long the bubble stays visible after a quick press
help: On a quick press the keyboard releases the key almost at once, so the bubble can be a flicker that you cannot see. The bubble stays after the release until it has been visible for this time. A value of 0 hides it the moment that you lift your finger.

title: Popup on key
name: keypress_popup_on_key_title
description: Grow the bubble upward from the pressed key itself
help:
On: the bubble sits on the key that you press and stretches upward. It is as wide as the key, with a large character near its top. This is the look of a stock keyboard.

Off: a small bubble floats above your fingertip, with a gap.

title: Popup font size
name: keypress_popup_font_size_title
description: Text size in the preview bubble and the alternate keys
help: This multiplies the text size inside the character bubble that appears while you press a key, and in the popup of alternate keys. The size of the key labels does not change.

title: Popup height
name: keypress_popup_height_title
description: Height of the key preview bubble
help:
This is the height of the character bubble. With "Popup on key" turned on, the keyboard measures it from the bottom of the key that you press. A bubble taller than the key goes above it and stays visible past your finger.

Each of the two bubble styles keeps its own height, because a floating bubble starts above the key and needs less of it. Turn "Popup on key" on or off, and this slider shows the height of that style.

title: Popup distance above key
name: keypress_popup_offset_y_title
description: How far the floating bubble sits above the key
help:
The floating bubble sits above the key that you press. If your finger covers it, raise this distance until you can read it.

This applies only while "Popup on key" is off. The on-key bubble grows out of the key itself, so it has no distance to set. Use "Popup height" for that style.

title: Popup sideways shift
name: keypress_popup_offset_x_title
description: Move the floating bubble left or right of the key
help:
Your hand covers one side of the key more than the other. Move the bubble away from that side and you can read it without moving your hand.

A negative value moves the bubble to the left. A positive value moves it to the right. Near the edge of the keyboard the bubble stops at the edge.

title: Popup color
name: keypress_popup_background_title
description: Background of the key preview bubble
help:
By default the bubble takes its color from the keyboard theme. Pick a color here and the bubble uses it instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

This is only the preview bubble. The alternate keys, the language list and the menus in the panels keep the color of the theme.

title: Popup text color
name: keypress_popup_text_color_title
description: Color of the character inside the bubble
help:
By default the character takes its color from the keyboard theme. Pick a color here and the character uses it instead. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

This is only the preview bubble, as with the popup color above.

title: Popup shape
name: keypress_popup_shape_title
description: Outline of every popup, from a square to a circle
help:
This is the outline of every popup that the keyboard draws: the character bubble, the alternate keys, the language list and the menus in the panels. Only the rounded and the cut shapes follow the corner radius below. The others size their corners from the popup itself.

A theme can carry its own shape. When it does, the theme wins over this setting.

title: Popup corner radius
name: keypress_popup_radius_title
description: How round the corners of a popup are
help:
This is the corner radius of every popup. A value of 0 gives square corners. A high value makes the corners fully round.

Only the rounded and the cut popup shapes use this value. A theme can carry its own radius, and it wins over this setting.

title: Press and hold hints
name: keypress_long_press_hints_title
description: Show the alternate character of each key in its corner
help: A small label in the top right corner of each key shows its first press and hold character. This is the digit, symbol or accent at the start of the popup. Keys that run a clipboard shortcut below show no hint.

title: All accents on press and hold
name: keypress_all_accents_title
description: Fill the popup of every letter with its full set of accents
help:
This adds the complete set of accents for each Latin letter (à á â ä ã å ā …) to its press and hold popup. The keyboard keeps the characters that the layout already lists.

This setting is off by default. The built-in popups are short on purpose, and the full set has many characters. It applies to letters only.

title: No accents on press and hold
name: keypress_no_accents_title
description: Take the accented letters out of every letter's popup
help:
This removes the accented forms of each Latin letter (à á â ä ã å ā …) from its press and hold popup, on every layout at once. The digits, symbols and shortcuts on the letters stay.

This setting is off by default. It only changes the popups: dictionaries and the text you type are untouched. When All accents on press and hold is also on, this one wins.

title: Top row press and hold
name: keypress_top_row_holds_title
description: What a hold on q to p types
help:
The letters q to p hold the digits 1 to 0. This picks what those holds type, whether or not the number row is on.

Auto keeps the digits while the number row is off and drops them while it is on, since the row already has them. Digits keeps them with the row on too. Symbols puts the symbols above each digit on a number row in their place: ! @ # $ % ^ & * ( ). None drops them either way, so those keys open with their accents or have no popup.

It applies to every layout that puts digits on its letters. To give one key a different character, edit its alternates in the layout editor. Auto is the default.

title: Your hold symbols
name: keypress_hold_symbols_title
description: Pick the symbol each letter holds, on every layout
help: Type a symbol under a letter and a press and hold on that letter offers it first, on every layout, in place of the symbol or digit the layout puts there; the corner hint shows it too. Leave a box empty to keep the layout's own. SwiftKey fills in the set SwiftKey uses.

title: Your language's letters first
name: keypress_native_letters_title
description: Put letters such as ü ahead of the number in the popup
help:
Most letter keys start their press and hold popup with a number or a symbol, such as 7 on u. With this on, the letters of the language you are typing move in front of it. In German, a hold on u then types ü, and ü is the small character in the corner of the key. The number stays in the popup, right after them.

The keyboard knows which letters belong to each language, so accents that your language does not use stay where they were. English uses no accented letters, so its keys do not change. A key whose popup you wrote yourself in the layout editor keeps the order you wrote. This setting is on by default.

title: Shifted letter on press and hold
name: keypress_shifted_popup_title
description: Add what each key types under shift to its popup
help:
This adds the character each key types under shift to the end of its press and hold popup. In Latin scripts that is the capital letter. In scripts with no capitals, such as Arabic or Devanagari, it is the other letter or mark on that key, so you can reach it without pressing shift. Layouts that draw their shifted keys on a page of their own, which includes most imported Keyman keyboards, take them from that page. A key that already lists it is left alone.

It also pairs with the swipe from the ?123 and ABC keys: that gesture types one key from another layer, and the shift key is on the layer your finger has left. This setting is off by default.

title: Press and hold ?123 for the number pad
name: keypress_symbols_numpad_title
description: Press and hold the symbols key to open the number pad
help: Normally the ?123 key only changes to the symbol layer. With this setting on, hold it to open the number pad panel over any field. You get a full number pad without leaving the current text box. A quick press still changes the layer. If your layout gives the ?123 key press and hold characters of its own, the hold opens them, and the number pad is an entry in that popup.

title: Press and hold enter for emoji
name: keypress_enter_emoji_title
description: Open the emoji panel from the enter key's popup
help:
With this setting on, holding the enter key opens a popup with an emoji entry at the front. With Choose without lifting on, a plain press and hold opens the emoji panel as soon as you lift your finger. A quick press still does what enter always does.

In a chat or search box, the same popup also has the line break that the Send or Search key replaces. Slide to it to use it. This setting is off by default.

title: Currency keys
name: keypress_currency_keys_title
help: These are the characters in the press and hold popup of the $ key, in order. Put your own currency first. Separate the characters with spaces. Keep the default (৳ € £ ¥ ₹ ₿), or clear the field to restore the built-in set.

title: Ctrl shortcuts as raw key events
name: keypress_ctrl_raw_title
description: For terminals. Off means that Ctrl+A, C, V and X use the clipboard
help:
A Ctrl key on a custom layout normally runs A, C, V and X through the clipboard actions of Android. Those work everywhere, including web pages and apps built with Compose.

A terminal needs the raw key event instead. There Ctrl+C means interrupt, not copy. The keyboard cannot tell the two apart, so this is a setting and not a guess.

title: Hold shortcuts
name: keypress_hold_actions_title
description: Edit actions in the press and hold popup of a letter key
help: Each action you pick goes into the press and hold popup of its key, after the accents that the key already has. Copy and cut take the selection, or all the text if you select nothing. Undo and redo send the same shortcuts as the toolbar tools. Choose the keys under Shortcut keys. To put the action nearer to the key, or first so that a plain press and hold runs it, use Action position.

title: Action position
name: keypress_hold_action_position_title
description: Where the shortcut goes in the press and hold popup
help:
The shortcut usually goes last in the popup, after the accents of its key. Move it nearer to the key here.

After 1 character: a plain press and hold still types the first accent, which is also the one the corner hint shows, and the shortcut is a short slide away.

First: a plain press and hold runs the shortcut straight away, and the accents move one along. Keep your finger down and slide onto the accent you want.

A place that is past all the accents of a key puts the shortcut last on that key. This needs Choose without lifting, under Alternate keys.

title: Slide from 🌐 for shortcuts
name: keypress_globe_drag_title
description: Press 🌐 and slide onto C to copy, V to paste
help: Put your finger on the 🌐 key, slide it onto a shortcut key and lift: onto A selects all, C copies, V pastes, X cuts, Z undoes and Y redoes. These are the same keys and the same actions as the hold shortcuts, and you can change the keys under Shortcut keys. This works when the hold shortcuts are off too. Lift anywhere else and nothing happens. Slide back onto 🌐 to change the language as a tap does. If you hold 🌐 still until the language list opens, the slide is for the list. This setting is off by default.

title: Auto theme
name: theme_auto_title
description: Use a light theme in the day and a dark theme at night

title: Change the theme
name: theme_shuffle_interval_title
description: How often a random half selects a new theme

title: Change the theme now
name: theme_shuffle_now_title
description: Select a new theme from your sets

title: Match the app colors
name: theme_app_colors_title
description: Use the colors of the app that you type in

title: Palette style
name: theme_app_colors_style_title
description: How one app color becomes a full palette

title: Import an icon pack
name: plugins_icons_import_title
description: Opens a .wmicons file that a person shared

title: Reset all icons
name: plugins_icons_reset_title
description: This turns the pack off and deletes every single-icon change. The app keeps the installed packs.

title: Key corner radius
name: appearance_key_corner_radius_title
description: How round the corners of the keys are
help: 0 gives square keys. 28 gives keys with a full pill shape.

title: Key label font size
name: appearance_key_label_size_title
description: Scale of the labels on the keys
help: This changes the size of every label on the keys. The popup bubbles have their own font size under Key press → Key popup.

title: Key hint font size
name: appearance_key_hint_size_title
description: Scale of the small hint character in the corner of each key
help: This changes the size of the small hint that the keyboard prints in the corner of a key. The keyboard shows the hint when "Press and hold hints" is on. Larger values make the hints easier to read. The default is ×1.00.

title: Key hint position
name: appearance_key_hint_offset_title
description: Distance of the corner hint from the top edge of the key
help: At 0 dp the hint touches the top edge of the key, and below 0 it moves up past the key's inner margin. Larger values move the hint down, nearer to the label. The default is 1 dp.

title: Key hint side position
name: appearance_key_hint_offset_x_title
description: How far in from the side of the key the hint sits. Below 0 moves it out to the edge

title: Key label across
name: appearance_key_label_offset_x_title
description: Moves the letter on each key to the side, away from a large hint

title: Key label up or down
name: appearance_key_label_offset_y_title
description: Moves the letter on each key down, or up below 0, away from a large hint

title: Reset pinned tools
name: home_reset_pinned_tools_title
description: Restore the default toolbar tools

title: Show the toolbar
name: appearance_toolbar_show_title
description: The strip above the keys that holds the suggestions and the tools
help: The toolbar is the row above the keys. It shows the word suggestions while you type. At other times it shows your pinned tools, such as emoji, clipboard and cursor keys. Turn it off to give its height to the keys. The app asks you to confirm, because this also hides the suggestions and every tool.

title: Where the tools go
name: appearance_toolbar_placement_title
description: Share the suggestion strip, or use a row above it
help: With "The strip", the tools and the suggestions share one row. The tools rest there, the suggestions take the row while you type, and the arrow button changes between them. This costs no height. With "A button", the arrow button opens a row of tools above the suggestions, and the button closes it again. With "Always", that row of tools stays open. Both of the last two keep the tools in reach while you type, and both use the height of one more row.

title: Suggestion strip
name: appearance_toolbar_show_strip_title
description: Keep the suggestion row above the tools row
help: Turn this off to remove the suggestion row and keep only the row of tools. The keyboard gets one row shorter. Useful if you have turned suggestions off and the row sits empty. Everything else that appears in that row goes too: the paste chip for your last copy, one-time codes, snippet offers and other chips. Voice typing's compact bar still shows there while you dictate.

title: Tools in landscape
name: appearance_toolbar_landscape_column_title
description: A column beside the keys while the phone is sideways
help: A phone on its side has width to spare and little height. Pick a side and, in landscape, the tools leave the top of the keyboard and stand in a column down that edge, next to the suggestions and the keys, always in reach. If the tools had a row of their own, its height goes back to the keys. The column follows the rest of the toolbar settings: your pinned tools in their order, their colors and labels, and how they fit. Portrait is unchanged.

title: Swipe down to hide
name: appearance_toolbar_swipe_down_title
description: Swipe down on the toolbar to close the keyboard
help: When this is on, a swipe down anywhere on the toolbar closes the keyboard. It is off by default, so the gesture does not start while you scroll or rearrange the toolbar. To move a tool you press and hold it, so that gesture does not close the keyboard.

title: Rearrange by dragging
name: appearance_toolbar_drag_title
description: Press and hold a tool on the toolbar, then drag it to a new place
help: When this is on, a press and hold that moves picks the tool up so you can drop it elsewhere on the toolbar. When it is off, a press and hold that moves stays a press and hold, and the toolbox is where you rearrange the toolbar. Turn it off if a hold keeps turning into a drag by accident.

title: Press and hold delay
name: appearance_toolbar_hold_delay_title
description: How long you hold a tool before the hold counts
help: This sets how long you press a tool on the toolbar or in the toolbox before the press counts as a hold. A hold runs the action you chose under Press and hold on the toolbar on the tool's own settings page, opens that settings page, or picks the tool up to move it. At System, the keyboard uses the touch and hold delay from your phone's accessibility settings.

title: Only the toolbar with a hardware keyboard
name: appearance_toolbar_hardware_only_title
description: When a hardware keyboard is connected, show only the toolbar
help: When you connect a Bluetooth keyboard or a dock keyboard, the on-screen keys go away and only the toolbar stays. Emoji, clipboard and the other tools stay one press away while you type on the hardware keyboard. A keyboard button at the end of the toolbar brings the keys back whenever you want them. This setting is off by default.

title: Hide the keys when I type on the hardware keyboard
name: appearance_toolbar_hardware_auto_hide_title
description: Keys you bring up with the toolbar's keyboard button go away at the next key you type
help: With only the toolbar showing, the keyboard button at the end of the toolbar brings the on-screen keys up, and the same button puts them away. With this on, typing on the physical keyboard puts them away too. Off, they stay until you tap the button again. Either way the keyboard remembers whether the keys were up for the next text box. On a physical keyboard, the shortcut leader and then Space does the same as the button. This setting is on by default.

title: Reverse the order for right-to-left languages
name: appearance_toolbar_rtl_title
description: Mirror the whole toolbar when you type a right-to-left script
help: For right-to-left scripts, such as Arabic, Hebrew and Persian, the whole toolbar goes from right to left, so it follows the text: the toolbox button moves to the right edge and the pinned tools run back from it. This setting is off by default, so that switching between a left-to-right and a right-to-left language leaves the tools where your fingers expect them. The toolbox grid does not change either way.

title: Tool layout
name: appearance_toolbar_fit_title
description: How the pinned tools share the toolbar
help: Fixed size keeps the tools at one size on the left. Spread out shares the full width of the toolbar between them, like the word suggestions do. Scroll keeps each tool at a comfortable size when you pin more than fit, and lets you swipe through them. You select the tools on the toolbar from the keyboard: open the toolbox with the grid button, then press and hold a tool and drag it between the toolbar and the toolbox. With Scroll, change the order from the toolbox, because a drag inside a toolbar that scrolls is difficult.

title: Toolbar top padding
name: appearance_toolbar_padding_top_title
description: Space above the tools and the suggestions
help: This adds space between the top edge of the keyboard and the toolbar. The default is 4 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount.

title: Toolbar bottom padding
name: appearance_toolbar_padding_bottom_title
description: Space between the toolbar and the keys
help: This adds space between the toolbar and the first row of keys. The default is 0 dp. The toolbar and the keyboard get taller by the same amount.

title: Hide the toolbar and the clipboard on the lock screen
name: appearance_toolbar_lock_title
description: Hide the top strip and block the clipboard while your device is locked
help: The keyboard opens over your lock screen when you answer a notification or use a search box there. This setting then hides the full top strip and blocks the clipboard panel. The strip holds the word suggestions and every pinned tool, so the clipboard tool and its paste chip also go. Copied text such as one-time codes and passwords stays off a screen that anyone can wake. This setting is off by default. When your device is unlocked, the keyboard does not change.

title: Tool labels
name: appearance_toolbar_labels_title
description: Show the name of each tool below its icon on the toolbar
help: The keyboard draws a small name below every pinned tool. Increase the toolbar height to give the labels space.

title: Label text size
name: appearance_toolbar_label_size_title
description: Font size of the tool labels on the toolbar

title: Keep labelled tools one width
name: appearance_toolbar_labels_fixed_title
description: Cut a long name short instead of widening its button

title: Color the pinned tools
name: appearance_toolbar_pinned_colors_title
description: Give the tools on the toolbar the colors they have in the toolbox

title: Suggestion text size
name: appearance_suggestion_text_size_title
description: How large the words in the suggestion strip are
help: Key labels have their own size setting and the suggestions above them did not, so large keys could still come with small suggestions. This also sizes the candidate row for Chinese, Japanese and Cantonese input, since it is the same row in a different mode. This setting is 100% by default.

title: Suggestion spacing
name: appearance_suggestion_spacing_title
description: The gap on each side of a word in the suggestion strip
help: Lower it to fit more of a long word before it has to shrink, or to pack more suggestions onto a narrow screen. Raise it to keep neighbouring words from reading as one when the strip scrolls. This setting is 6 dp by default.

title: Autocorrect word color
name: appearance_suggestion_primary_color_title
description: Color of the word that autocorrect will put in for a space
help: The strip draws its first suggestion in bold. Pick a color here and that word takes the color only when autocorrect has decided to put it in for you when you type a space. A bold word without the color is the top suggestion, and a space keeps what you typed. The other suggestions keep the theme color. Reset the row to follow the theme again.

title: Tool circle radius
name: appearance_tool_circle_title
description: How round the circle behind each toolbar tool is
