help: 20 draws a full circle behind every tool icon, like Gboard. Smaller values give rounded squares. 0 removes the background and leaves only the icons.

title: Tool background shape
name: appearance_tool_shape_title
description: Outline of the shape behind each toolbar tool

title: Tool background width
name: appearance_tool_width_title
description: Width of the shape behind each toolbar tool
help: 38 keeps the classic circle. Wider values stretch it into a pill, like Gboard. The background only shows when the tool circle radius is above 0. Pairs well with the scrollable toolbar.

title: Tool icon size
name: appearance_tool_icon_size_title
description: Size of the icon inside each tool button
help: Applies to the toolbar and the toolbox grid. The buttons keep their size, so the same number of tools still fit. 22 is the default.

title: Reset toolbar
name: appearance_toolbar_reset_title
description: Put every setting on this screen back to its default

title: Toolbox layout
name: appearance_toolbox_layout_title
description: How the toolbox draws its tools
help: Icons is a grid. It shows a round icon for each tool with the name below it. Pills gives each tool a wide row with round ends. The icon is on the left and the name is beside it. An arrow on the right marks the tools that open something, such as Themes and Clipboard. The other tools do their work immediately, such as Flashlight and Undo. Fewer tools fit on the screen, but you can read every name.

title: Toolbox grid size
name: appearance_toolbox_columns_title
description: Tools in each row of the toolbox grid
help: The toolbox is the grid behind the grid button on the toolbar. Fewer tools in a row makes each tool larger and easier to press. More tools in a row shows more tools without a scroll.

title: Pills per row
name: appearance_toolbox_pill_columns_title
description: How many tool pills go side by side
help: The default is two. One gives every tool the full width, which is good for long names and large text. Three works only in landscape or on a tablet. On a smaller screen the names get cut.

title: Fill the pills with the tool color
name: appearance_toolbox_pill_filled_title
description: Color the full pill and not only its icon
help: When this is off, each pill keeps the background of the theme and only the icon shows the color of the tool. When it is on, the pill gets that color. The icon and the name change to a color that you can read on it: white on most colors, almost black on pale colors. This needs "Colorful tool icons" (Settings → Tools) to be on. With that setting off, there is no color to fill the pill with.

title: Swipe the toolbox in pages
name: appearance_toolbox_paginate_title
description: Fixed pages that you swipe sideways, and not one grid that scrolls
help: When this is off, the toolbox is one grid that scrolls up and down. When it is on, the toolbox becomes pages that you swipe between. Dots below the grid show your position. Every tool then keeps the same place, so you can find it from memory. To move a tool to another page, drag it and hold it against the side edge of the toolbox until the page turns.

title: Tools per page
name: appearance_toolbox_page_size_title
description: How many tools each toolbox page holds
help: Select a multiple of your row size to fill the last row of every page. If you select more tools than the panel can show, the page scrolls as well as swipes.

title: Reset toolbox order
name: appearance_reset_toolbox_order_title
description: Put the tools in the toolbox grid back in their original order

title: Toolbox order
name: appearance_toolbox_sort_title
description: Put the tools in your own order, or the ones you use first
help: Your order is the order you make by dragging tools around the toolbox. Most used puts the tools you open most often first. Recently used puts the tool you opened last first. Tools you have never opened come after them, in your order. The toolbox sorts itself each time it opens, so tools do not move while you tap them. A folder sits where its first tool falls, and keeps its own order inside. Dragging a tool still changes your order, and you get it back when you choose Your order again.

title: Toolbox label size
name: appearance_toolbox_label_size_title
description: The name under each tool in the full tool panel
help: By default these follow the toolbar label size, so the two agree. Set a size here to make the toolbox names larger or smaller on their own. This setting follows the toolbar by default.

title: Space around each tool
name: appearance_toolbox_cell_spacing_title
description: Above and below each tool in the toolbox grid. Less fits more rows on a page

title: Back puts a tool's keys down first
name: appearance_toolbox_back_lowers_title
description: The next Back closes the tool

title: Toolbox search
name: appearance_toolbox_search_button_title
description: A search button on the toolbar while the toolbox is open
help: While the toolbox is open, the toolbar shows a search button. Tapping it opens the search over the whole keyboard, with a back button that returns to the toolbox. Type a tool's name to find it, wherever it is, folders included. Turn this off to leave the toolbox without a search.

title: Search button at the far end
name: appearance_toolbox_search_at_end_title
description: Put the toolbox search at the far end of the toolbar, away from the back button
help: When this is on, the search button sits at the far end of the toolbar, after your pinned tools, so a tap meant for the back button does not open the search. When it is off, the search button sits right next to the back button.

title: Search order before typing
name: appearance_toolbox_search_sort_title
description: How the toolbox search lists the tools until you type
help: The toolbox search lists every tool until you type something. Your order lists them the way you arranged the toolbox. Most used puts the tools you open most often first. Recently used puts the tool you opened last first. Once you type, the names that start with what you typed come first.

title: Reset toolbox
name: appearance_toolbox_reset_title
description: Put every setting on this screen back to its default

title: Photo services
name: photo_providers_section_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone

title: Rotate the background
name: photo_rotation_on_title
description: Turn it off to keep the photo that is up now

title: Change the photo now
name: photo_rotation_shuffle_title
description: Go to the next photo

title: Photo collection
name: photo_rotation_source_saved_title
description: The photos you added yourself

title: Online photos
name: photo_rotation_source_online_title
description: New photos from Unsplash and Pexels

title: Subjects
name: photo_rotation_topics_title
description: Optional

title: Safe photos only
name: photo_rotation_safe_title
description: Tell the service to remove adult photos

title: Wide photos only
name: photo_rotation_wide_title
description: A keyboard is wide and short, so wide photos fit better

title: Use mobile data
name: photo_rotation_metered_title
description: Get photos when there is no Wi-Fi

title: Photos to keep ready
name: photo_rotation_pool_title
help: More photos make the background repeat less frequently, but the app uses more storage. The app keeps the photos on the device, so the background changes also when there is no network.

title: Delete the photos that the app got
name: photo_rotation_delete_downloads_title
description: The app will get a new set at the next change

title: Add from this device
name: photo_add_device_title
description: The app copies each photo, so it stays available

title: Symbols on shift
name: layout_number_row_shift_symbols_title
description: Press and hold shift to change the digit row to symbols
help: While you hold shift on the letter layout, the number row shows the fill row of the symbol layer (= \\ < > [ ] { } | ~) instead of the digits. You reach those symbols with one shift, and you do not change to the symbols layer. On the second symbols layer, the number row already shows more arrow and comparison symbols.

title: Number row in symbols
name: layout_number_row_in_symbols_title
description: Keep the digit row on the ?123 symbols layer too
help: The digit row stays in place when you change to the symbols layer. This is the default. Turn it off to drop the digits from the ?123 layer and keep them on the letters, where the number row is already showing them. The symbols keep their bracket and maths row, so nothing but the digits goes, and the keyboard is one row shorter on the symbols layer.

title: Symbol row on number pads
name: layout_number_row_on_keypad_title
description: Keep the row above the keypad in number and phone fields
help: A number, phone, date or time field gets a keypad, which already leads with the digits, so the number row carries symbols instead: + * # , ; ( ) - / . on a phone field, and + - * / = ( ) % : . on the others. This is the default. Turn it off to type on the bare keypad, one row shorter. The digit row over the letters is not affected.

title: Arrow keys row
name: layout_arrow_row_title
description: Show left, up, down and right keys under the keyboard
help: The keyboard adds a row of four arrow keys under the spacebar, so you can move the cursor without the toolbar or a drag on the spacebar. Hold an arrow to keep moving. The row is as tall as the number row, and the keyboard grows by that much.

title: Arrow order
name: layout_arrow_row_order_title
description: Drag the handles to put the arrows in the order you want
help: The keys appear on the row from left to right in the order of this list.

title: Go back to the letters
name: layout_symbols_return_title
description: Leave ?123 after you type one of these characters
help: You change to ?123 for one full stop or one question mark, and the keyboard changes back to the letters after it. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer until you press ABC. The emoji panel has the same setting.

title: Characters that go back
name: layout_symbols_return_chars_title
help: Type the characters that send the keyboard back to the letters. Spaces between them are optional. An empty box uses the default characters ! ? . , ; and :. Digits are not in the default set, because you usually type more than one digit at a time.

title: Go back after a space
name: layout_symbols_return_space_title
description: Leave ?123 when you press the spacebar
help: You type a number or a symbol on ?123, press space, and the keyboard changes back to the letters for the next word. Turn this off to stay on the symbols layer, for example to type a phone number with spaces in it. This works on its own, with or without Go back to the letters.

title: Type native digits in
name: layout_numeral_scope_title
description: Where the keyboard types the native digits
help: You select the digit glyphs for each language under Languages → the language → Numerals. This setting controls where the keyboard also types those glyphs. "Text fields" is the default. It types 0-9 in number, phone, date and time fields, which keeps them machine-readable. In all other fields it types the native digits. "Everywhere" types the native digits in those fields too. "Display only" shows the glyphs on the keys but always types 0-9.

title: Key layouts
name: langemoji_lang_keymaps_title
description: Edit, add and delete layouts

title: Comma key opens emoji
name: layout_comma_emoji_title
description: Replace the comma key with an emoji key
help: The comma key on the bottom row becomes an emoji key, and the comma moves into the press and hold alternates. This also deletes the emoji tool from the toolbar, because the key replaces it. Drag the tool out of the toolbox again if you want both.

title: Press and hold enter for emoji
name: keypress_enter_emoji_title
description: Open the emoji panel from the enter key's popup
help:
With this setting on, holding the enter key opens a popup with an emoji entry at the front. With Choose without lifting on, a plain press and hold opens the emoji panel as soon as you lift your finger. A quick press still does what enter always does.

In a chat or search box, the same popup also has the line break that the Send or Search key replaces. Slide to it to use it. This setting is off by default.

title: 1234 key on the symbol pages
name: layout_symbols_numpad_key_title
description: A key after ABC that opens the number pad
help: The symbol pages get a 1234 key directly after the ABC key, as in Gboard. Press it to open the number pad panel over the current field. The spacebar gets narrower by one key to make room. A layout that already has a number pad key, or a symbol page you arranged by hand in the layout editor, does not change.

title: Show the 🌐 key
name: layout_show_globe_title
description: Turn off to give its space to the spacebar
help: When this is off, the 🌐 key is not on the bottom row of any layout. If "Emoji key instead of 🌐" is on, the emoji key in that position goes too. The spacebar gets the space. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to "Language" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default.

title: 🌐 goes back to the last language
name: layout_globe_recent_title
description: Tap quickly to go further back
help: When this is on, one tap on the 🌐 key goes back to the layout you used before this one, and the next tap comes back again. This is useful with many languages when you only type two or three of them at a time. Tap several times quickly to go further back, most recently used first. A list shows where you are. When this is off, each tap goes to the next layout in your switch order. This also changes the language key on a physical keyboard. This setting is off by default.

title: Ignore 🌐 right after typing
name: layout_globe_guard_title
description: A tap on 🌐 just after a letter does nothing
help: The 🌐 key is next to the spacebar and the comma, so a fast thumb can hit it by mistake in the middle of a word and change the language. Set a time here and a tap on 🌐 that comes sooner than this after a typed key does nothing. A tap after a pause changes the language as usual, and so do quick taps one after the other on 🌐 itself. Press and hold 🌐 to open the language list at any time. Letters, space, backspace and enter count as typing. Shift and the mode keys do not. This setting is off by default.

title: Emoji key instead of 🌐
name: layout_globe_emoji_title
description: Replace the language key with an emoji key
help: The 🌐 key on the bottom row opens the emoji panel and does not change the language. You can still change the language from the spacebar. Set a swipe to "Language" under Typing → Gestures. A short swipe does this by default. Turn this off to get the 🌐 key back.

title: Swap the comma and 🌐 keys
name: layout_swap_comma_globe_title
description: Put the comma next to the spacebar
help: The two keys on each side of the spacebar change places. If one of them is an emoji key, it moves to the outer position and the comma stays next to the spacebar. Turn this off to get the usual order.

title: Keep the 🌐 key in one place
name: layout_globe_in_one_place_title
description: The same place on every layout, beside the spacebar
help: Some layouts put the 🌐 key in a different place, for example at the far left, or directly after the ?123 key. This moves it to the place the built-in layouts use, so your thumb finds it in the same place in every language. The keys to its left get wider or narrower to make room, and the spacebar changes to fit. A layout where that would make keys too small is left as it is, and so is a second layout you open from a key. Turn this off to see every layout as its author made it.

title: Import a layout
name: layout_editor_import_title
description: Opens a .wmlayout.json file that someone shared

title: Panel layouts
name: panel_layouts_title
description: The panels every layout uses unless it has a panel grid of its own. Each layout's editor has a tab for every panel.

title: Add tablet keys automatically
name: layout_editor_tablet_expand_title
description: On a tablet, add tab, backslash, caps lock, a second shift and the arrow keys around this layout

title: Number row
name: layout_number_row_title
description: Show a row of digits above the letters
help: The keyboard adds a row of digits from 1 to 0 above the letter keys, so you do not press and hold for a digit. The digits on the press and hold of the top letter row are not available while this is on. The keyboard becomes one row taller.

title: Number row height
name: layout_number_row_height_title
description: The height of the digit row, separate from the letter keys
help: A short digit row keeps fast access to the numbers. It adds less height to the keyboard than a full row.

title: Resize by dragging
name: layout_resize_drag_title
description: Opens the keyboard with handles on its edges: drag the height, position and side margins in place

title: Key height
name: layout_key_height_title
description: The height of each key row, which sets the total keyboard height
help: Tall keys are easier to press, but the keyboard covers more of the screen. The emoji, clipboard and snippet panels change size with this value too.

title: Bottom row height
name: layout_bottom_row_height_title
description: The height of the space and enter row on its own
help: The bottom row holds the spacebar and enter. Give it a height that is taller or shorter than the letter keys, to get a larger spacebar without a taller keyboard. "Follow keys" is the default and keeps the bottom row the same height as the other rows. Custom layouts that set their own row heights ignore this setting.

title: Left padding
name: layout_side_padding_left_title
description: Move the left edge of the keyboard toward the centre
help: The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the left. The keys move toward the middle for thumb reach, and the keyboard does not dock to one edge as one-handed mode does. The default is 0 percent. This setting applies on top of the keyboard width above.

title: Right padding
name: layout_side_padding_right_title
description: Move the right edge of the keyboard toward the centre
help: The keyboard keeps this much of the screen width clear on the right. Set it to the same value as the left padding for an even margin, or to a different one to shift the keys toward the hand you type with. The default is 0 percent.

title: Key spacing
name: layout_key_spacing_title
description: The gap between the keys
help: This changes the space around each key. A larger value moves the keys apart and makes the keyboard a little taller, because the gap is part of each row. A smaller value moves the keys closer together. The default is 100 percent.

title: Extend edge keys into the gaps
name: layout_extend_edge_keys_title
description: A tap in the blank space at the end of a short row, or below the bottom row, types the nearest key
help: Some rows are shorter than the keyboard, for example the A to L row of QWERTY. They have blank space at the left and right ends. With this setting on, a tap in that space types the key at that end of the row, so a tap to the left of A types A. Also, a tap in the space below the bottom row types the key above it, so a tap below the space bar types a space. The keys do not change size or position. Only the area that you can tap gets larger. This setting is on by default.

title: Keyboard scale
name: layout_keyboard_scale_title
description: Make the whole keyboard smaller or larger on this screen

title: Bottom padding
name: layout_bottom_padding_title
description: More space below the keys, above the navigation bar
help: The whole keyboard moves up, away from the bottom edge and the gesture navigation bar. Increase it if the bottom row is too near the edge of the screen, or if you start the system navigation by mistake.

title: Hide the system keyboard bar
name: layout_hide_system_keyboard_bar_title
description: Remove the bar with the hide and switch keyboard buttons below the keys
help: With gesture navigation, Android puts a bar below the keyboard. It has a button that hides the keyboard and a button that changes to a different keyboard. With this setting on, the keyboard asks Android to remove that bar. When the bar is gone, the keys move down into its space. If the keys still sit higher than you want, make Bottom padding smaller. To hide the keyboard, use Back. To change to a different keyboard, use the 🌐 key. Only Android 16 and later lets a keyboard remove the bar. On older versions, this setting is not available. With three-button navigation, or on phones that draw the bar as part of the system navigation bar, no keyboard can remove it, so the setting is not available there either. This setting is off by default.

title: Round top corners
name: layout_board_corner_top_title
description: Cut round corners into the top of the keyboard

title: Round bottom corners
name: layout_board_corner_bottom_title
description: Cut round corners into the bottom of the keyboard

title: Keyboard width
name: layout_keyboard_width_title
description: Make the keyboard narrower
help: Below 100 percent the keyboard does not fill the whole screen. Select the edge that it sits at below. This helps on very wide screens. One-handed mode below is a quick preset, and it replaces this value while it is on.

title: Keyboard position
name: layout_keyboard_position_title
description: Where the narrow keyboard sits: at the left edge, in the centre, or at the right edge.
help: Where the narrow keyboard sits: at the left edge, in the centre, or at the right edge.

title: One-handed mode on this screen
name: layout_variant_allow_one_handed_title
description: When off, the keyboard stays full width here, even with one-handed mode on

title: Split keyboard on this screen
name: layout_variant_allow_split_title
description: When off, the keyboard stays in one piece here, even with split keyboard on

title: Follow portrait again
name: layout_follow_portrait_title
description: Delete the sizes that you set for %1$s

title: One-handed mode
name: layout_one_handed_title
description: Make the keyboard smaller at one edge of the screen

title: Portrait only
name: layout_one_handed_portrait_only_title
description: Use the whole width when the phone is sideways
help: One-handed mode is one setting for both orientations, so a keyboard made small for a thumb in portrait stays small after you turn the phone, where you may want a split keyboard instead. Turn this on to keep one-handed mode in portrait and switch it off in landscape. Turn the phone back and it comes back. This setting is off by default.

title: Split keyboard
name: layout_split_title
description: Divide the keys into a left half and a right half
help: The keyboard divides each row in the middle and puts a gap between the halves, so your thumbs move less on wide screens. This helps most on tablets, foldable devices and phones in landscape. By default the keyboard also divides the spacebar between the two halves.

title: Split gap
name: layout_split_gap_title
description: The width of the gap between the halves
help: This is the gap in the centre, as a percentage of the keyboard width. A larger gap moves the halves toward the edges, but each key becomes narrower.

title: Split the spacebar
name: layout_split_spacebar_title
description: Divide the spacebar too, or keep it as one key across the gap
help: When this is on, the spacebar is divided between the two halves like every other row, and the centre of the bottom row is empty. When this is off, the spacebar stays as one key and fills the gap, so both thumbs can press it where they meet. The other keys on the bottom row stay in their halves. This setting is on by default.

title: Floating keyboard
name: layout_floating_title
description: Put the keyboard in a panel that you can move while the phone is upright
help: The keyboard becomes a small panel that floats above the apps, and it does not dock to the bottom of the screen. Drag the pill on the panel's handle bar to move it. Drag the corner grip to change the size. Press the dock button to go back to the normal keyboard. Apps do not change size while the panel floats, and touches outside the panel go to the app. Portrait and landscape each remember their own choice, so the floating tool and the dock button only change the one the phone is held in.

title: Floating in landscape
name: layout_floating_landscape_title
description: Float the keyboard while the phone is sideways
help: Turn this on and off on its own to float the keyboard sideways and keep it docked upright, or the other way round. The keyboard changes as soon as you turn the phone. Until you change one of the two, landscape follows the portrait switch.

title: Full-screen typing in landscape
name: layout_landscape_fullscreen_title
description: Type into a text box that covers the app
help: When you hold the phone sideways, Android normally replaces the app with a large text box and a Done button while you type, because the keyboard leaves little room. Turn this off to keep the app in view above the keyboard, as in portrait. Some apps turn the text box off on their own. Tablets and unfolded phones never use it. This setting is on by default.

title: Handle bar position
name: layout_floating_handle_title
description: Where the floating panel's drag bar and resize grip sit
help: The handle bar holds the dock button, the drag pill and the resize grip. Under the keys is the default, where your thumb already is. With the bar under the keys, drag the grip down to make the panel taller. With the bar above the keys, drag it up.

title: Floating keyboard width
name: layout_floating_width_title
description: You can also drag the corner grip of the panel
help: This is the width of the floating panel. The key heights still follow the sliders above.

title: Keep the keyboard on screen
name: layout_persistent_title
description: Stay open when no text field has focus
help: After the keyboard opens, it stays on screen when the text field closes, and over apps that have no text field. This lets you send keys and keyboard shortcuts to an app, for example to set a hotkey in a notes app. To close the keyboard, press the hide key, swipe down on the toolbar, or press Back. It opens again the next time you tap a text field. The keyboard never stays on the lock screen. Works docked or floating.

title: Show the floating button
name: floating_button_enable_title
description: A small round button floats over every app
help: A small round button floats over every app, with the keyboard open or closed. Tap it, double tap it or press and hold it, and it does what you set below: open the keyboard, even on a screen with no text field, start voice typing, ask the AI about the screen, or open any tool. Press and hold opens a quick menu of more actions round the button; slide onto one and let go to run it. Drag the button to move it, and it settles against the nearer side. Drag it onto the cross at the bottom of the screen to hide it until the keyboard next opens or closes. Needs Android's Display over other apps permission.

title: Let the button read the screen
name: floating_button_screen_title
description: Ask AI can bring the text on screen with it, and Look up can find the word you tap, once the screen reading service is on

title: Add an action
name: floating_button_menu_add_title
description: Up to %1$d actions

title: Show names
name: floating_button_menu_labels_title
description: Each action's name under its icon. Off, only the one under your finger is named

title: Distance from the button
name: floating_button_menu_gap_title
description: How far out the actions sit, in the quick menu and in every category

title: Reset the menu
name: floating_button_menu_reset_title
description: Voice typing, Ask AI, clipboard, emoji and the keyboard

title: Shape
name: floating_button_shape_title
description: The outline of the button and of its actions

title: Size
name: floating_button_size_title
description: How large the button is

title: Opacity
name: floating_button_opacity_title
description: How solid the button is while you use it

title: Fade when idle
name: floating_button_idle_title
description: How long the button waits before it fades

title: Faded opacity
name: floating_button_idle_opacity_title
description: How solid the button is once it fades

title: Tuck into the edge
name: floating_button_tuck_title
description: A faded button slides half off the side, out of the way of the app

title: Show while typing
name: floating_button_while_typing_title
description: Stay on screen above the open keyboard, where a tap on the keyboard action closes it

title: Float over the keyboard
name: floating_button_over_keyboard_title
description: Stay where you put it, even over the keys. Only the button takes a touch; the keys around it still type

title: Hide in landscape
name: floating_button_landscape_title
description: Keep games and videos clear of the button

title: Vibrate on touch
name: floating_button_haptics_title
description: A tick on a tap, a firmer one when the menu opens or an action is picked

title: Reset position
name: floating_button_reset_position_title
description: Back to the right edge, a little below the middle

title: Use the keyboard's share sheet
name: share_sheet_enabled_title
description: Shares from the keyboard and this app open it. Off uses Android's share sheet
help: The sheet lists every app that takes the share, the same apps Android's sheet lists. It shows no contacts, because only Android's own sheet can read those. More options on the sheet opens Android's sheet when you want them.

title: Show recent apps
name: share_sheet_recents_title
description: The apps you shared to last lead the sheet. Off forgets them

title: Unpin all apps
name: share_sheet_pins_title
help: Hold an app on the sheet to pin it or take it off the recent row.

title: Remember language per app
name: langemoji_lang_per_app_toggle_title
description: Open each app with the layout that you used there last
help: When you change language while you type in an app, the keyboard remembers your choice for that app. The keyboard uses that language again the next time that you type there. You can change language with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. Apps where you selected no language use your last language. A field that requires Latin letters, such as a password box, still overrides this. A field that gives its own language also overrides this.

title: List languages in the Android switcher
name: langemoji_lang_os_switcher_title
description: Add each language to the input method switcher of the system
help:
The keyboard registers every layout that you turn on as an Android input method subtype. The "Choose input method" sheet of the system then lists them, and you can change between them there. Turn this off to keep language switching inside the keyboard only, with the 🌐 key, a spacebar swipe or the picker. The keyboard then tells the system only the language that you type in, and the sheet lists it as "WM Keyboard" instead of as one language name. A system spell checker that uses the system language then checks the language that you type in.

To register a language and to make it switchable are two different things. Android lists only the languages that something turns on. Until then, Android selects them itself from the languages of your device, and it usually selects one. On Android 14 and newer, the keyboard turns them all on for you. On older versions, select them by hand in the system settings with the row below.

title: Carry the word over
name: langemoji_lang_carry_word_title
description: Switch to a phonetic layout mid-word and the letters that you typed convert too
help: Phonetic layouts such as Avro, Hindi phonetic and Khipro spell their script with roman letters. When you notice halfway through a word that you are still on your Latin keyboard, switching language now converts the letters that you already typed instead of leaving them as they are: type "tu", switch to Avro, and the word reads তু, so "mi" after it finishes তুমি. Turn this off if you often switch language right after an English word and before typing a space, because that word is carried over as well.

title: Extra stop in the switcher
name: langemoji_lang_switcher_extra_title
description: After your languages, holding or swiping the spacebar can reach the language settings or your other keyboards
help: Hold the spacebar and the preview above it lists your languages. With this set, one more stop follows the last of them: a gear that opens this screen, or a keyboard that opens Android's list of keyboards. Drag onto it and lift to go there. A swipe along the spacebar reaches it too. A quick flick still moves one language at a time, so only a swipe that keeps going past your last language lands on it. With two languages, the swipe then walks three stops in a line instead of toggling. The list and carousel pickers show the gear as a row of their own, next to Other keyboards.

title: Show app name first
name: langemoji_lang_app_name_first_title
description: The label reads "WM Keyboard · <language>"
help: This puts the app name in front of the language in the label of the switcher. Android decides how it styles the label and the app name, such as which one is bold or grey. This setting changes only the label text, not that styling.

title: Select languages in the system settings
name: langemoji_lang_subtype_enabler_title
description: The list of Android. Use it only if the switcher looks wrong

title: Conjunct-aware backspace
name: languages_conjunct_backspace_title
description: Delete a whole cluster like %1$s as one unit
help: Backspace usually deletes one code point at a time. This sometimes leaves half-formed clusters on the screen. With this setting on, one press deletes the whole cluster while you type %1$s. Other languages keep their own setting.

title: Tap twice for আ or এ
name: languages_bengali_vowel_twice_title
description: On Probhat, Jatiya and BSTI, after a vowel: one tap gives য়া or য়ে, a second tap gives আ or এ
help: After a vowel, the আ-কার and এ-কার keys write য়া and য়ে, as in কায়া and দিয়ে, because a bare া or ে cannot follow a vowel. With this on, pressing the key again straight away turns য়া into আ and য়ে into এ. Holding either key offers আ or এ whether this is on or not. Off by default, because a quick double press then types the glide twice.

title: Show the letter each key types
name: languages_translit_hints_row_title
description: Put the %1$s a key is about to write in its corner

title: Keep the first two words in place
name: languages_phonetic_strip_fixed_title
description: What you typed first, the %1$s word next, then suggestions
help:
Usually the first word on the strip is the word that the space bar will write, so the words move as you type.

With this on, the first two words always stay in the same place. On the left is what you typed, in English letters. Next to it is the %1$s that the phonetic rules make from it, letter for letter. The suggestions come after them. Tap the left word to write in English, or the word next to it to write the exact %1$s reading.

The space bar does not change: it writes the same word as before. That word shows in bold, and in the autocorrect word color if you set one. The strip does not put a word in the middle on this layout, so that the left word is always first.

title: Show the keys you pressed
name: languages_raw_keys_chip_title
description: prshn/ next to প্রশ্ন on the strip
help:
Khipro keys such as f and / change the letters before them, so the word on the strip does not always show which keys you pressed.

With this on, the second word on the strip is the keys exactly as you pressed them, modifiers included. Tap it to write those keys as they are, in English letters. The space bar does not change: it writes the Bengali word.

With this off, the keys show only when they are all letters and English is mixed in on the layout, for English words that the dictionary does not know.

title: Suggestions after them
name: languages_phonetic_strip_source_title
description: Which language fills the rest of the strip

title: Avro candidate list
name: languages_phonetic_candidates_title
description: The words desktop Avro shows under the word you type
help:
Desktop Avro shows a short list under the word you type. The list is built the same way here. First comes the known spelling for what you typed, if there is one. Next come the %1$s dictionary words that sound like it, and the words made by adding an ending to one of them, such as বন্ধু + দের. The words closest to the letter-for-letter reading come first. Last is the letter-for-letter reading itself.

In the suggestion strip: the word that the space bar will write stays first, and the list follows it. Bar above the strip: the whole list goes in a row of its own above the strip, and you can scroll through it. The row stays while the layout is on, so the keyboard does not change height between words.

The space bar writes the same word with all three choices.

title: Neural suggestions
name: languages_neural_phonetic_title
description: Up to three more readings of the word from a small AI model, after the word the space bar writes. %1$s to download, shared by every language
help:
IndicXlit, a model by AI4Bharat, has learned from millions of words how people write %1$s in Latin letters, so it often knows the word when the spelling is loose, such as valobashi or bhalobasi for ভালোবাসি.

Its readings come right after the word the space bar will write. That word never changes, and the model never corrects anything by itself: tap one of its readings to use it. Readings that are in the word list come first. Let it choose the word, below, changes that for spellings the keyboard has no word for.

The model runs on the phone, and nothing you type leaves it. One download covers Bengali, Hindi, Urdu, Assamese, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam.

title: Let it choose the word
name: languages_neural_leads_title
description: When the rules spell no known word, the space bar writes the model's best reading from the word list
help:
The space bar usually writes what the phonetic rules spell. When that is not a word in the %1$s word list or among your own words, and the known-spellings list has nothing for what you typed, this lets the model's best reading that is in the word list go first instead, so a space writes it. The rules' spelling comes right after it in the strip, one tap away.

On test words the space bar wrote the right word 56%% of the time instead of 25%% in Bengali, and 49%% instead of 41%% in Hindi. The cost: a name or a rare word spelled exactly by the rules, but missing from the word list, can come out as a listed word that looks like it. About one such spelling in six did in Bengali, one in fifteen in Hindi. Words the list knows are left alone.

title: Full guide
name: languages_phonetic_guide_title
description: Every rule with examples, on the WM Keyboard website

title: Allow ANSI output
name: languages_ansi_allowed_title
description: An ANSI button on the Bengali layouts writes Bijoy-style text, so আ comes out as Av
help:
ANSI is how Bengali was written before Unicode, in Bijoy and in fonts like SutonnyMJ: each Bengali letter is stored as a Latin character, and the font draws it as Bengali. Some design software and older documents still need it.

With this on, every Bengali layout gets an ANSI button beside the suggestions. Tap it and what you type goes into the text box as ANSI, so আমার সোনার বাংলা becomes Avgvi †mvbvi evsjv. Tap it again for Unicode.

The word you are typing shows as Unicode until you finish it. ANSI text only reads as Bengali in an ANSI font, so keep the button off everywhere else.

title: ANSI version
name: languages_ansi_version_title
description: Pick the one your ANSI font is made for
help: The ANSI fonts do not all put the letters in the same places, so there are three versions. Version 2 is the common one, used by SutonnyMJ and most Bijoy fonts. If the text comes out as the wrong letters in your font, try another version.

title: Allow Zawgyi output
name: languages_zawgyi_allowed_title
description: A Zawgyi button on the Burmese layouts writes text for Zawgyi fonts
help:
Zawgyi is the font encoding most Burmese text was written in before Unicode, and many phones, apps and friends still use it. It uses the same characters as Unicode but puts them in a different order, so text written for one reads as broken letters in the other.

With this on, every Burmese layout gets a Zawgyi button beside the suggestions. Tap it and what you type goes into the text box as Zawgyi. Tap it again for Unicode. Suggestions, autocorrect and the word list keep working in Unicode while you type.

The word you are typing shows as Unicode until you finish it. When the text box already holds Zawgyi, the keyboard offers to write Zawgyi there even with the button off.

title: Unicode key font
name: languages_zawgyi_key_font_title
description: Draw the Burmese keys in Noto Sans Myanmar, for a phone whose own font is Zawgyi
help:
A phone set up for Zawgyi has a Zawgyi font in place of its Myanmar font, and that font shows Unicode letters in the wrong order. The keyboard's keys and suggestions are Unicode, so on such a phone they can look broken.

With this on, the keyboard draws Burmese in its own copy of Noto Sans Myanmar, a Unicode font, whatever font the phone uses. The font is downloaded once from WM Keyboard's data repository (195 KB) the first time the keys need it. A Myanmar font you picked under Appearance still comes first.

title: Fancy style
name: languages_fancy_style_row_title
description: The lettering the fancy keyboard types. Also switchable from the strip over the keys.

title: Add a font
name: languages_fancy_fonts_add_title
description: Paste an alphabet and type in it from the strip

title: Only tone real syllables
name: languages_vietnamese_strict_tones_title
description: A tone key is a letter unless the word is one the language spells
help: Telex and VNI mark a tone whenever the vowels allow it, so typing fas gives fá even though f is not a Vietnamese onset and there is no word there. With this on, a tone key that would land on something that is not a word is typed as the letter it is drawn as instead, and only a syllable the language actually spells takes a tone. mix is still mĩ, because that is a word.

title: Fill in left-out marks
name: languages_vietnamese_restore_marks_title
description: With the Vietnamese word list, tieng becomes tiếng when it can only be one word
help: Telex and VNI type only the marks you spell. With this on, a word you finish without one of its marks gets it from the Vietnamese word list, but only when the list has one way to read it: tieng becomes tiếng and duong becomes đường. A word the list already has is never changed, and a spelling like toan, which can be toàn, toán or toản, stays as you typed it. One backspace takes the change back. This needs autocorrect on and the Vietnamese word list on the device.

title: Numeral system
name: languages_numeral_system_title
description: The digits that the number row and the keypad show while you type %1$s
help: You select the digits for %1$s: its own digits, which are %2$s, or 0-9. This applies to this language only. The keys always show the digits that you select. To set where the keyboard also types them, open Layout & size, then Numerals.

title: Custom dictionaries
name: languages_custom_dictionaries_title
description: Import your own word lists

title: Dictionaries
name: languages_dictionaries_title
help: Each item works offline after the download. The checkbox turns an item off and keeps the file. Delete removes the file from the device.

title: Traditional characters
name: languages_cjk_traditional_title
description: The keyboard converts candidates to Traditional (繁體). With the phrase table pack, it converts word by word, so 头发 becomes 頭髮.
help: The keyboard converts each candidate from Simplified (简体) to Traditional (繁體) before it shows the candidate. Some Simplified characters have more than one Traditional form, and the word decides which one is correct: 发 is 發 in 發展 but 髮 in 頭髮, and 后 is 後 in 後來 but 后 in 皇后. With the phrase table pack downloaded, the keyboard reads whole words, so it writes the correct form. Without the pack, or for a word that is in no table, it converts one character at a time.

title: Show the reading in the text field
name: languages_cjk_reading_in_field_title
description: Off, the pinyin you type shows only on the keyboard, before the candidates
help: On, the pinyin, zhuyin or Jyutping that you type shows underlined in the text field until you pick a candidate. Off, the text field stays as it is, and the keyboard shows what you typed at the start of the candidate strip. Only the candidate you pick goes into the text field, the way fcitx5 works.

title: Engine
name: languages_rime_engine_title
description: With RIME, the layouts of this language convert through the RIME schema you pick for each. The keys stay the same.

title: Import RIME schemas
name: languages_rime_import_title
description: A zip with .schema.yaml and .dict.yaml files, such as a schema from GitHub. They are compiled with the packs.

title: Japanese engine
name: languages_mozc_engine_title
description: With Mozc, every Japanese layout converts through Mozc: romaji, flick, 12-key and kana. The keys stay the same. The arrow keys resize the part of the reading being converted.

title: Forget what Mozc learned
name: languages_mozc_clear_title
description: Clears the conversions, predictions and reading boundaries Mozc learned from your picks. The dictionary stays.

title: Import from FlorisBoard
name: languages_cjk_flex_import_title
description: Read a FlorisBoard language pack (.flex). It can fill the Cangjie and stroke tables above.

title: Lazy pronunciation (懶音)
name: languages_cjk_lazy_title
description: Match merged sounds: n↔l, ng↔∅, gw→g before -o, -ng↔-n, -k↔-t…

title: Match kana without marks
name: languages_cjk_loose_marks_title
description: かつこう also finds 学校 (がっこう)
help: On the Flick and Kana JIS layouts, a small kana, a ゛ or a ゜ is an extra key. With this on, a plain kana also matches those forms: か finds が, つ finds っ and づ, は finds ば and ぱ, や finds ゃ. When two words are almost equally common, the one that you typed exactly comes first. A kana that you typed with a mark is not changed, and Romaji typing is not changed.

title: Full-width space
name: languages_cjk_full_width_space_title
description: The space bar types a full-width space [　]
help: Japanese and Chinese text is spaced with the ideographic space (U+3000), which is as wide as one character. With this on, the space bar types it instead of the narrow space used between words in other languages. A space pressed while you are still typing a reading picks a candidate as before, and only a press with nothing waiting to convert types a space.

title: Space steps through candidates
name: languages_cjk_space_steps_title
description: Space highlights the next candidate, and Enter types it
help: Off, the space bar types the first candidate straight away. On, the first press highlights it and each press after moves to the next one, the way Japanese input methods work. Enter types the highlighted candidate, typing on keeps it and starts a new reading, and backspace goes back to the reading. With a physical keyboard, the arrow keys move the highlight either way, Enter or space types it, and once something is highlighted the keys 1 to 9 pick a candidate and Escape goes back to the reading.

title: Jianpin (简拼)
name: languages_cjk_jianpin_title
description: Type only the first letter of a syllable: wm finds 我们, zg finds 中国
help: A letter that is not a whole syllable stands for every syllable that starts with it, so wm finds 我们 and haod finds 好的. Each letter is one syllable: hd means h… plus d…. A syllable that you type in full is matched exactly and ranks first. The letters z, c and s also cover zh, ch and sh. A Double Pinyin scheme does not use this, because every syllable is exactly two keys there.

title: Next-word suggestions (联想)
name: languages_cjk_prediction_title
description: After you pick Chinese text, show the words that usually come next
help: When a conversion is complete and nothing is composing, the strip shows the words that usually follow the text before the cursor. Tap one to type it, and the strip shows what follows that. The words that you write after others come first, then the common word pairs, then the rest of a word that the last character starts (无 gives 聊). This needs the word pairs pack.

title: Date, time and numbers
name: languages_cjk_shortcuts_title
description: rq types the date, sj the time, xq the weekday, v and a number gives Chinese numerals
help: Type rq for the date, sj for the time and xq for the weekday. These show after the best candidate for the same letters. Type v and then a number, for example v1234.5, to get it as 一千二百三十四点五, as 壹仟贰佰叁拾肆点伍 for amounts, or digit by digit. No pinyin syllable starts with v, so this does not change pinyin.

title: Fuzzy Pinyin
name: languages_cjk_fuzzy_title
description: Match confusable sounds: zh↔z, ch↔c, sh↔s, n↔l, an↔ang, in↔ing…

title: Custom Double Pinyin scheme
name: languages_cjk_double_pinyin_custom_title
description: Set your own keys. Copy, paste, import or export the scheme, in the same format as fcitx

title: Emoji button in toolbar
name: langemoji_emoji_toolbar_title
description: Open emoji with one press from the top bar
help: The emoji button stays visible in the top bar, also while the suggestions show. The emoji panel has a tab for each category. You can search in English and Bengali, and in any language that you add a keyword pack for. Press and hold an emoji for the skin tone variants.

title: Buttons beside the suggestions
name: langemoji_strip_shortcut_title
description: Tools that stay in the top bar while the suggestions show. Drag to change their order

title: Toolbox button
name: langemoji_strip_toolbox_title
description: Put the toolbox first among these buttons, so it is one tap away while the suggestions show

title: Buttons on the right
name: langemoji_strip_at_end_title
description: Put these buttons after the suggestions, at the far end of the strip

title: Own size for these buttons
name: langemoji_strip_own_size_title
description: Size the buttons beside the suggestions apart from the toolbar's tools

title: Button width
name: langemoji_strip_tool_width_title
description: How wide each button beside the suggestions is

title: Button icon size
name: langemoji_strip_icon_size_title
description: How big the icon in each button beside the suggestions is

title: Full-screen emoji panel
name: langemoji_emoji_full_bleed_title
description: Hide the toolbar and move the category tabs up, next to a back button
help: The emoji panel fills the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row go away. The category tabs move into the row that they leave, next to a back button. Turn this off to keep the toolbar in reach while you select emoji.

title: Panel layout
name: panel_layout_row_title
description: Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel

title: Emoji suggestions
name: langemoji_emoji_prediction_title
description: Show emoji while you type. The word birthday suggests 🎂 🎉 🥳
help: Emoji that match appear at the end of the suggestion strip while you type. This works in English and in any language whose keywords you have. %1$s also suggests 🎂.

title: Press an emoji suggestion
name: langemoji_emoji_insert_mode_title
description: What happens to the word that you typed. Hold the suggestion for the other one
help:
"Replace word" changes the word that you typed to the emoji. If you type birthday and press 🎂, only 🎂 stays, as in Gboard. "Keep word" adds the emoji after the word: birthday 🎂.

Hold an emoji suggestion to do the other one this time. With "Replace word" selected, a hold keeps the word. With "Keep word" selected, a hold replaces it.

title: Emoji row
name: langemoji_emoji_row_title
description: A row of your own emoji, like Gboard

title: Emoji row content
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_content_title
description: Favourites always come first

title: Emoji in the row
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_count_title
description: How many fit across. A higher number packs them tighter
help: The row divides its width into this many slots and makes the emoji small enough to fit them. A higher number gives smaller emoji that are closer together. When scrolling is off, the row hides the emoji after the last slot. When scrolling is on, a swipe shows them.

title: Scroll the emoji row
name: langemoji_emoji_bar_scroll_title
description: Swipe sideways for the emoji after the visible ones
help: When this is on, and it is on by default, you can swipe the row sideways to reach the emoji after the visible ones. When this is off, the row does not move. It shows only the emoji that fit, so a sideways swipe cannot move it under your finger.

title: Emoji font
name: langemoji_emoji_font_title
description: How emoji look on the keyboard itself
help: "System" uses the emoji pack of your device. On Samsung devices that is the Samsung set. "Google" downloads Noto Color Emoji, the standard Android look, one time through the system font provider, and keeps it on your device. "Installed" uses an emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. "Custom" uses one emoji font file that you import below. The text that you send is always plain Unicode. Other apps and other devices draw it with their own emoji font.

title: Default skin tone
name: langemoji_emoji_skin_tone_title
description: For toned emoji in the panel, the suggestions and the search
help: The keyboard shows toned emoji (👍, 🙏, 🧑…) with this Fitzpatrick tone in the grid of the emoji panel, the suggestion strip and the emoji search results. It also inserts them with that tone. An emoji that you selected a tone for keeps your tone while "Override with last used" is on. The first option (✋) keeps the neutral yellow base.

title: Override with last used
name: langemoji_emoji_tone_override_title
description: Use the tone that you selected last for an emoji, not the default
help: When this is on, and it is on by default, an emoji that you already selected a tone for keeps that tone everywhere: in the panel, the suggestions and the search. You select that tone from the press and hold popup of the emoji in the panel. The emoji does not use the default above. When this is off, the default skin tone always wins.

title: Hide emoji that your device cannot show
name: langemoji_emoji_hide_unrenderable_title
description: Skip emoji that show as a blank box in the panel, the search and the suggestions
help: Older devices, and some brands, have an emoji font that is older than the newest emoji. Those emoji then show as an empty "tofu" box. This setting hides every emoji that the emoji font of your device cannot draw. To see them all, set the emoji font above to "Google" (Noto Color Emoji). You can also install a complete emoji font from Addons, such as Twemoji or OpenMoji. WM Keyboard has no emoji font of its own. It uses the font that you select here.

title: Find any character by its Unicode name
name: langemoji_emoji_unicode_search_title
description: The emoji search also finds symbols, letters and marks by the words of their name
help: Type the words of a character's Unicode name in the emoji search and it appears after the emoji: em dash, copyright sign, greek small letter lambda, latin small letter a with ogonek. Every character of the Basic Multilingual Plane is covered, which is tens of thousands of letters, marks and symbols. Tapping one inserts it. This setting is off by default.

title: Grid size
name: langemoji_emoji_grid_size_title
description: How wide each cell of the emoji grid is, at least. A smaller size fits more columns
help: The emoji panel fits as many columns as its width allows, and each cell is at least this wide. A smaller size packs more emoji on one screen. A larger size spreads them out, and each one is easier to hit. When the emoji size below needs more room than this, the cells grow to fit it.

title: Narrowest tab
name: langemoji_emoji_tab_width_title
description: How narrow a category tab may get before the tabs scroll sideways. Less fits every tab on the screen

title: Emoji size
name: langemoji_emoji_size_title
description: How large the emoji panel draws each emoji
help: The size of the emoji in the grid of the emoji panel, on every tab and in the search results. The cells always keep enough room around each emoji, so a very large size can also mean fewer columns. The press and hold popup keeps its own size.

title: Columns
name: langemoji_emoji_grid_columns_title
description: How many emoji go across one row
help: Auto fits as many columns as the grid size allows, so a wider screen shows more. A fixed number keeps each emoji in the same column on every screen. Arrange like sets this to match the keyboard you pick.

title: Row height
name: langemoji_emoji_grid_row_height_title
description: How tall each row of emoji is
help: Auto makes each row as tall as the emoji size needs. A fixed height, with fixed columns, makes the same swipe scroll to the same emoji as on the keyboard that Arrange like copied.

title: History tab
name: langemoji_emoji_tab_mode_title
description: What the first tab of the emoji panel shows
help: "Recent" lists emoji in the order that you used them last. "Most used" puts the emoji that you use most often first. The keyboard always keeps your favourite emoji at the start of both lists. "Off" removes the tab, so the panel opens on the first emoji category.

title: Clear recents button
name: langemoji_emoji_clear_recents_title
description: A button on the Recent tab that deletes the recents list
help: This adds a "Clear recents" button to the Recent tab of the emoji panel. It is off by default, to keep the tab clean.

title: Kaomoji tab
name: langemoji_emoji_kaomoji_title
description: A tab of text faces: ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯ and :-)
help: This adds a Kaomoji tab at the end of the tabs of the emoji panel. Kaomoji are Japanese style faces, such as (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻. Emoticons are the Western ASCII ones, such as :-D and <3. Both are in one library that you can change: add your own faces, put them under tags, and sort them. If you press a face, the keyboard types it as plain text. It does not go into your emoji history.

title: Emoji descriptions
name: langemoji_emoji_long_press_name_title
description: Show the name of the emoji at the top of its press and hold popup
help: Press and hold an emoji to show its Unicode name, such as "skull and crossbones". The name appears above the favourite control and the variant controls. This helps you to see the difference between emoji that look almost the same.

title: Animated emoji
name: langemoji_emoji_animated_title
description: Send a moving version of an emoji from its press and hold popup
help: Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to see the moving version, and a control that sends it as an image. The images are Noto Animated Emoji by Google, under the CC BY 4.0 licence. The keyboard downloads each one from Google when you ask for it, at about 800 KB. About 880 emoji have one, and the control does not appear for the others, or in an app that accepts no images.

title: Send emoji as image
name: langemoji_emoji_sticker_title
description: Add a control that sends the emoji itself as a picture
help: Press and hold an emoji in the emoji panel to get a control that sends it as a picture, in the emoji font that you selected. This is useful when the other person has a device that draws the emoji differently, or cannot draw it at all. The keyboard draws the picture on your device and downloads nothing, except one time for the Google emoji font. The picture goes out in the same way as the stickers of the sticker tool. To change that, open Tools, then Stickers, then "Send stickers as". The control does not appear in an app that accepts no images.

title: Return to the keyboard after you insert
name: langemoji_emoji_close_after_insert_title
description: Close the panel when you insert one emoji or paste one clip
help: By default, the emoji panel and the clipboard panel stay open, so that you can select several items. Turn this on to go back to the keys directly after one emoji or one clipboard paste.

title: Switch to GIFs and stickers
name: langemoji_media_switcher_title
description: Where the emoji, GIF and sticker panels show the buttons that go between them
help: The switch has one button for each of the emoji panel, the GIF panel and the sticker panel, so that you can go from one to the next directly. It is at the same place in all three panels. "Bottom" puts it in the bottom row, between ABC and the space bar. "Top" puts it at the end of the search row. The GIF button and the sticker button show only while those tools are on. If you changed the layout of the emoji panel, the switch is where your layout puts it. To add it, use the "Emoji, GIF and sticker switch" part in the panel layout editor.

title: Open the last used panel
name: langemoji_media_remember_title
description: The emoji key opens emoji, GIFs or stickers, the same as you left them
help: When this is on, the emoji key and the emoji tool open the panel of the three that you used last. If one of the three panels is open, they close it. When this is off, the emoji key always opens the emoji panel. The keyboard forgets the last panel when it restarts.

title: One long list
name: langemoji_emoji_continuous_title
description: Scroll through all the emoji, with a heading over each category
help: When this is on, the emoji panel is one list that you scroll from top to bottom. Each category starts with its name, and you go from one category to the next without a stop. The category tabs jump to a category and show the category that you are in. When this is off, each category is a page, and you swipe left or right to go to the next one.

title: Panel height
name: langemoji_panel_height_title
description: How much taller than the keyboard the emoji, GIF and sticker panels open
help: A taller panel shows more emoji, GIFs and stickers at one time. The letters keep their own height, and the three panels have the same height, so the keyboard does not move when you go from one to the next. The panel never covers more than most of the screen, so on a short screen, or with the phone sideways, it can stay shorter than this.

title: Add a source
name: emojimix_add_title
description: An address

title: Over the emoji panel
name: emojimix_panel_strip_title
description: Pick an emoji to see a row of mixes with it

title: On the suggestion strip
name: emojimix_typing_title
description: When the text ends in one or two emoji

title: Replace the emoji
name: emojimix_replace_title
description: Sending a mix removes the emoji it was made from

title: Mixes panel
name: emojimix_panel_title
description: A tab beside emoji, GIFs and stickers to put any two emoji together

title: Send as
name: emojimix_send_title
description: Apps that take no stickers get a picture

title: Fetch lists again each month
name: emojimix_auto_refresh_title
description: Only on a connection that is not metered

title: Separate Emoticons tab
name: langemoji_kaomoji_split_title
description: Show :-) and the other ASCII faces in a tab of their own

title: Tag tabs
name: langemoji_kaomoji_tag_tabs_title
description: A row of tags at the top of the tab. Off shows one long list with a heading for each tag.

title: Open on
name: langemoji_kaomoji_start_title
description: The tag the tab shows when you open the emoji panel

title: Edit buttons
name: langemoji_kaomoji_rail_title
description: A column of buttons beside the faces: search, add, edit and tags
help: With the column off, the add, edit and tags buttons move to the end of the tag row, so you can still change your faces from the keyboard.

title: Kaomoji suggestions
name: langemoji_kaomoji_suggest_title
description: Type a tag, such as shrug or tableflip, to see its faces in the suggestions
help: The keyboard shows the faces of a tag when the word you type is the name of that tag. Your favourites and the faces you use most come first. If you press one, it goes in after your word, or in place of it, the same as an emoji suggestion.

title: Kaomoji in emoji search
name: langemoji_kaomoji_in_search_title
description: Show the faces that match after the emoji in the search of the emoji panel

title: Import
name: langemoji_kaomoji_import_title
description: An Emotic export, a file from this keyboard, or a list with one face on each line

title: Export
name: langemoji_kaomoji_export_title
description: Save your faces and tags to a file

title: Reset the library
name: langemoji_kaomoji_reset_title
description: Go back to the faces that come with the keyboard

title: Use voice typing
name: voice_enabled_title
description: Off removes the microphone from the whole keyboard
help: When this is off, the keyboard never opens the microphone. The Voice tool goes from the toolbar, the toolbox and the shortcuts, the boxes of the keyboard itself lose their microphone button, and the collapsed bar does not show. The recognition engines and the Whisper models are not loaded, so voice typing uses no memory. Your voice settings stay as they are for when you turn it on again.

title: Recognition engine
name: voice_engine_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The system recognizer is fast and shows the words while you speak, but it depends on the operating system and its languages. Offline Whisper runs fully on your device across many languages and sends no audio anywhere. It transcribes each phrase after you stop speaking. Offline Whistle works the same way with one small, fast model for seven languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch and Polish. Offline Asr4All is English only, and writes the words while you speak, on your device. Offline Parakeet transcribes 25 European languages and works out which one you speak. Offline Moonshine is a small, quick model for English. A transcription server does the same work on a computer you choose, so your phone spends less battery. The recording of each phrase goes to that server and nowhere else.

title: Voice typing language
name: voice_languages_title
description: The language dictation listens for, or several at once

title: Engine for each language
name: voice_engine_languages_title
description: Pick an engine and a model for each of your languages
help:
Each language can use its own engine. For example, English can use the system recognizer and Bangla an Offline Whisper model. A language set to the default uses the recognition engine above.

Only the models on your phone are listed. Download more on the page of each engine.

title: Voice typing view
name: voice_ui_title
description: What the microphone button opens
help: The panel gives large controls and status in the space of the keyboard. The compact bar speaks over the keys, so you can correct words as they land. The collapsed bar hides the whole keyboard behind a small pill that you can drag anywhere, and it stays until you bring the keyboard back. The panel and the compact bar have a collapse button, and the pill has an expand button, so you can switch styles without coming back to this screen.

title: Language button on the compact bar
name: voice_strip_language_title
description: Pick the voice typing language without leaving the bar
help:
Adds a small button with the language code, such as EN, to the compact bar over the keys. Tap it to choose which language voice typing listens for: the keyboard's language, one language whatever the keyboard is set to, or all your keyboard languages at once. It is the same choice as the button on the full voice panel.

This setting is off by default, because the bar has room for one line. The button shows only when you have more than one keyboard language, or a language already chosen.

title: Voice typing mode
name: voice_typing_title
description: How voice typing and the keys share the field
help:
One block at a time is the usual way. The words appear in the field while you speak, and the first key press stops the microphone.

Type while you speak keeps the microphone open. Each phrase goes into the field when you stop for breath, so the keys, the layouts and the suggestion strip stay live all through the session. Use it with the compact bar over the keys. This mode always keeps listening.

Plain text works the same way, but it adds no punctuation and no spaces. You control all of them from the keyboard. Use it for code, for terminals and for any field where you want only the words you said.

The two type-while-you-speak modes need the keys on screen, so they are offered only when the voice typing view is the compact bar over the keys. Plain text also needs the system recognizer: the offline models and a transcription server add their own punctuation.

title: Hold the tool to pick a mode
name: voice_hold_picks_title
description: Press and hold the Voice tool on the toolbar to choose a voice typing mode and start at once
help: A press and hold on the toolbar's Voice tool opens a menu of the three voice typing modes. Picking one makes it the mode and starts dictation straight away, so switching between one block at a time and typing while you speak is one hold rather than a trip through settings. Tap the tool to stop. Turn this off to give the hold back to the toolbar: it then runs the tool you bound to it, or opens this screen.

title: Reopen voice typing where you left it
name: voice_resume_title
description: Close the keyboard with voice typing open, and it opens listening next time
help:
When the keyboard goes away with the voice panel, the compact bar or the collapsed bar on screen, the next text field you tap opens on the same view and starts listening.

To stop that, leave voice typing before you close the keyboard: press Back or the close button on the panel or the compact bar, the keyboard button on the collapsed bar, or the Voice tool. The keyboard then opens on the keys as usual until you start voice typing again. Password fields always open on the keys.

title: Pause media during voice typing
name: voice_pause_media_title
description: Pause music and video while the microphone listens
help: When voice typing starts, the keyboard asks other apps to pause their sound. Music, podcasts and video stop while the microphone listens. They continue a moment after voice typing stops. An app that ignores the request continues to play.

title: Microphone switch
name: voice_mic_switch_title
description: Pick the microphone, and switch it from the voice panel
help:
On, you can choose a microphone below, and a button on the voice panel and both voice bars shows the microphone in use and switches to the next one that is connected.

Off, voice typing always listens through the microphone Android picks. The keyboard does not move the audio to a headset, and the button is gone.

title: Microphone
name: voice_mic_title
description: Prefer a Bluetooth, wired or USB microphone when one is connected
help:
Which microphone voice typing listens through. Automatic uses the one Android picks, which is a plugged-in headset before the phone. Pick a kind to prefer it whenever one is connected. When it is not connected, voice typing uses the automatic choice.

Offline Whisper and the transcription server can use every kind. The system recognizer records the audio itself, so for it only Bluetooth has an effect.

The microphone button on the voice panel and both voice bars shows the microphone in use. Tap it to switch to the next one that is connected.

title: Change engine from the voice tool
name: voice_engine_picker_title
description: A chip on the voice panel picks the engine and model for the language you dictate in
help: Shows a chip in the bottom left corner of the voice panel. It names the engine that the language you dictate in uses. Tap it to pick another engine or model for that language. Only the models on your phone are listed. The pick is the same as the one under Engine for each language.

title: Hold to talk
name: voice_hold_title
description: How long you hold the microphone before it becomes press-and-hold
help: A short tap on the microphone starts dictation and leaves it running until you tap again. Holding it instead dictates only while you hold, like a walkie-talkie. This is the line between the two. Raise it if a slow press keeps stopping your dictation, lower it if you mean to hold and it keeps latching on.

title: Keep listening
name: voice_continuous_title
description: Start the next sentence automatically after each one goes into the field

title: Stop after a pause
name: voice_silence_stop_title
description: End a Whisper or server clip by itself when you stop talking
help: Offline Whisper and the transcription server record a whole clip, so the microphone stays open until you press it or the clip fills: 30 seconds, or two minutes for a whisper.cpp model. Set a pause here and the clip ends by itself once you have said something and then gone quiet for that long. Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual hear the pause with the Phrase end detector. With Keep listening off, that also ends dictation, so you never have to reach for the microphone. The system recognizer stops after a pause of its own and ignores this. Off by default.

title: Phrase end detector
name: voice_vad_title
description: How Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual hear that you stopped talking
help: Asr4All, Sherpa and Omnilingual write while you speak, so they listen for the end of what you say themselves: that is when Stop after a pause counts, and where Omnilingual cuts its phrases. Silero VAD is a small network that tells speech from other sound; every Sherpa and Omnilingual model carries a copy, and Asr4All can download one. FireRedVAD is a newer network that its makers measured ahead of Silero in 102 languages, with far fewer false alarms; a 2.3 MB download. Loudness only uses no model at all: anything loud enough counts as speech, the way the pause stop works for Whisper and the server, so a noisy room can keep it listening. Your own model takes a Silero or TEN VAD file. A detector that cannot run yet falls back to Auto, which is Silero where it can run and loudness everywhere else.

title: Speech threshold
name: voice_vad_threshold_title
description: Lower hears softer speech, higher stops sooner in noise
help: How sure the detector must be that a moment is speech. Lower keeps listening through soft or distant speech, but noise can hold the phrase open. Higher ends the phrase sooner in a noisy room, but a quiet voice can be taken for silence. For Loudness only it sets how loud counts as speech: 50% is the level the pause stop has always used. 50% by default.

title: Smart Turn
name: voice_smart_turn_title
description: End sooner when you sound finished, wait longer when you do not
help: At each pause, Smart Turn v3.2 listens to the last 8 seconds and judges whether you finished what you were saying or stopped mid-thought, from how you said it: the falling voice at the end of a sentence, a word left hanging, an "um". When you sound finished, the phrase ends after a short pause; when you do not, it waits out the whole pause set in Stop after a pause. So you can set a long pause and still not wait at the end of every sentence. It was trained on 23 languages and is an 8.7 MB download that runs on ONNX Runtime. Off by default.

title: Reduce background noise
name: voice_denoise_title
description: Clean up the microphone before an offline model hears it
help: Takes background sound such as traffic, a busy café or a fan out of the microphone's audio before an offline engine (Whisper, Whistle, Asr4All, Parakeet, Moonshine, Sherpa, Omnilingual) hears it. Light is RNNoise, a tiny network that adds about 10 ms. Strong is DPDFNet, a DeepFilterNet model on ONNX Runtime: a 9 MB download, more work for the phone and 40 ms of delay, but it is the one that helps recognition. On noisy test recordings Light cost Whisper words, and Strong won some back. Without its model, Strong runs as Light. The system recognizer and the transcription server get the microphone as it is. Off by default.

title: Spoken punctuation
name: voice_punctuation_title
description: Say "comma", "question mark" or "দাঁড়ি" to type the mark

title: Add punctuation and capitals
name: voice_auto_punctuation_title
description: Full stops, commas, question marks and capitals for Sherpa and Omnilingual
help: Sherpa and Omnilingual write the words they hear and nothing else: no full stops, no commas, no capitals. With this on, a punctuation model reads each finished phrase on the phone and puts in full stops, commas and question marks in the marks of the language (। in Bengali and Hindi, ؟ in Arabic, 。 in Chinese), with a capital at the start of every sentence. Names get their capitals from the keyboard's word lists, and English ones also from Sherpa's English punctuation model when you have it. The model knows 88 languages and is a 151 MB download; English works without it if the English model is on the phone. Engines that punctuate for themselves are never touched, nor is plain voice typing.

title: Tidy dictation with AI
name: voice_ai_tidy_title
description: Remove filler words, repeats and spoken corrections from each phrase
help: After each phrase goes into the field, the keyboard sends it to the model of the AI tool. The model removes filler words such as um and uh, false starts, repeated words and the parts that you corrected aloud: "at three, no, four" becomes "at four". Your words, language and tone stay the same. The phrase stays as you said it if the answer is slow or fails, or if you change the text first. The next phrase starts when the answer arrives. Each phrase goes to the AI provider that you set for the AI tool. Plain text mode, password fields and the boxes of the keyboard itself are not tidied.

title: Recognition service
name: voice_system_service_title
description: Which app does the recognising

title: Prefer on-device recognition
name: voice_system_on_device_title
description: Use the speech model on your phone when it has one for the language
help:
On Android 12 and later the system recognizer can run on your phone when the language model is installed. If the model on the phone hears nothing at all, the keyboard switches that language to the recognizer service until the keyboard restarts.

Turn this off to always use the recognizer service. That service can send the audio over the internet while you speak.

title: Translate to English
name: voice_translate_title
description: Speak any language and type its English translation

title: Compute
name: models_whisper_compute_title
description: Where the GGML models run. Automatic uses the GPU for Base and larger models
help: This applies to the GGML models only. The LiteRT models always run on the CPU. The GPU reads speech faster on phones with a Qualcomm Snapdragon chip (an Adreno GPU), mostly with the larger models, where reading a phrase takes the most time. Other GPUs are not used. The first use of the GPU after an install or update can take some seconds while the GPU prepares. If the GPU does not start, has not enough memory for the model, or stops during a phrase, the app gives that phrase to the CPU, and from then on the CPU runs the model on this phone.
