Select GPU again to try it again. Automatic keeps the Tiny models on the CPU, which is about as fast for them.

title: Send the keyboard language
name: voice_server_language_title
description: Tell the server which language you are typing in. Turn this off to let the server detect it

title: Listen for my words
name: voice_bias_personal_title
description: Names and other words from your dictionary, so they are spelled your way
help: Each time you dictate, the keyboard sends a list of your own words with it: the words you added by hand, the words in Android's personal dictionary, and the words the keyboard learned from your typing that are not in any word list, such as names. The system engine also gets permission to use what it knows about your phone, such as your contacts. The list goes to the engine that listens to your voice, and nowhere else. The system engine uses it on Android 13 and later, if the engine supports it. A transcription server gets it as part of its prompt, Offline Whistle as words to favour, the whisper.cpp models of Offline Whisper as their prompt, and Offline Sherpa as words to boost (only the words its model can spell). The older LiteRT models of Offline Whisper cannot use a list.

title: Clipboard history
name: clipboard_history_title
description: Save copied text so that you can paste it quickly

title: Panel layout
name: panel_layout_row_title
description: Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel

title: Full-screen clipboard panel
name: clipboard_full_bleed_title
description: Hide the toolbar behind a back button so the history gets the whole keyboard
help: The clipboard panel takes the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and a slim back header takes their place. The history then shows more clips at once. While you search the history, the panel returns to its compact form so the keys fit below it. This setting is on by default.

title: Panel height
name: clipboard_panel_height_title
description: How much taller than the keyboard the clipboard panel opens
help: You can also drag the bar on top of the clipboard panel up or down. A taller panel shows more clips, so there is less to scroll. The panel never covers more than most of the screen, so on a short screen, or with the phone sideways, it can stay shorter than this. The default is the keyboard's own height.

title: Height over the keys
name: clipboard_over_keys_height_title
description: How much taller a panel opens when the keys are under it
help: This is the height of the clipboard when it is stacked over the keys or while you search it. Other panels with the keys under them use the same height: a snippet or dictionary search, a GIF search, a note that you write, and more. You can also drag the bar on top of such a panel up or down. The keys under the panel keep their size. The default is the compact height of each panel.

title: ABC, space and enter keys
name: clipboard_key_row_title
description: A row of keys along the bottom of the clipboard panel
help: Paste a link and press enter to go to it, or paste more clips with a space or a new line between them, without going back to the keyboard. ABC goes back to the letters. If you changed the panel layout, this setting does nothing: add the keys in the layout editor instead. The row is not shown while the clipboard is stacked over the keys. This setting is off by default.

title: History layout
name: clipboard_view_title
description: Cards in columns, or one clip per row
help: The grid packs cards in columns, which suits pictures. Set how many under Grid columns. The list gives each clip a whole row, which suits long text. The switch beside the panel's search bar changes the same setting. The grid is the default.

title: Grid columns
name: clipboard_columns_title
description: How many columns of cards the grid has
help: More columns show more clips at once, which suits short text. Fewer give each card more room, which suits long text and pictures. The list layout always shows one clip per row. The default is 2.

title: Lines per clip
name: clipboard_lines_title
description: How much of each clip's text the panel shows
help: Auto shows six lines on a grid card and three in a list row. Set a number to show that many lines in both layouts. Text that is longer ends with …. Tap the clip to paste all of it, or press and hold it to read the details.

title: Line spacing
name: clipboard_line_spacing_title
description: The space between the lines of a clip's text
help: At 100% the lines of a clip sit as close as the font allows. Raise it to spread them out. The default is 130%.

title: Time on each clip
name: clipboard_time_title
description: Show when a clip was copied, or how long it has left
help: Time copied shows how long ago you copied each clip. Time left shows how long each clip stays before the clipboard expiry deletes it. A pinned clip, or a clip in a history that never expires, shows no time left. This setting is off by default.

title: Number the clips
name: clipboard_numbers_title
description: Show a number beside each clip, so you tap the one you mean
help: Each clip keeps its own number while you search. The results show the numbers the clips had, and the count does not start again from 1. The numbers follow the order of the panel, from the top. This setting is off by default.

title: Pinned and unpinned tabs
name: clipboard_pinned_tabs_title
description: Show unpinned clips and pinned clips on two different tabs
help: The panel opens on the Unpinned tab. When you pin a clip, it moves to the Pinned tab. A search looks through the two tabs. With the tabs on, Pinned entries last has no effect. This setting is off by default.

title: Outline pinned clips
name: clipboard_outline_pinned_title
description: Draw a thin border in the accent color around each pinned clip

title: Pin and delete buttons
name: clipboard_card_buttons_title
description: Show a pin and a bin on every clip
help: With this setting off, press and hold a clip to pin or delete it from its popup. A card also loses the row the buttons sat on, unless the row still shows the clip's number, its time or a rich text tag, so more clips fit in the panel. This setting is on by default.

title: Clip shortcut button
name: clipboard_card_shortcut_title
description: What the small button at the end of a clip does
help: Edited mark shows a pencil on a clip you edited, and does nothing when pressed. Nothing hides it. Edit puts an edit button on every clip you can edit, so you do not have to press and hold the clip first. Select starts selecting clips with that one, for Combine, Tidy or Delete. QR code puts a QR button on every text clip, which opens the QR code tool on the clip's text, ready to send as a picture. Edited mark is the default.

title: Type out pasted clips
name: clipboard_type_out_title
description: Paste a clip one character at a time, as if typed
help: The text appears letter by letter, the way a one-time code goes into a row of code boxes. A clip longer than 200 characters is pasted all at once. Codes are typed out either way, from the One-time codes setting. This setting is off by default.

title: Move a pasted clip to the top
name: clipboard_bump_on_paste_title
description: A clip you paste from the history goes first in it, and back on the system clipboard

title: Rich text tag
name: clipboard_type_tags_title
description: Mark a clip that was copied with formatting
help: A clip copied with bold, links or other formatting shows a small Rich text label under its text. Turn this off to hide the label. A card with nothing else on that row then loses the row, so more clips fit. This setting is on by default.

title: Keep formatting
name: clipboard_keep_rich_text_title
description: Store copied text with its bold, links and other formatting
help: With this setting on, a copy that came with formatting pastes it back into apps that take formatting. Turn it off and every copy is kept as plain text from then on, so it pastes as plain text everywhere and never shows the Rich text label. The panel then shows every clip as plain text too: a link is not coloured, underlined or given an icon. Clips already in the history keep what they have. This setting is on by default.

title: Swipe to delete
name: clipboard_swipe_delete_title
description: Swipe a clip sideways to delete it
help: With this setting off, a sideways swipe on a clip does nothing, so a clip can't be lost to a swipe made while you scroll. Press and hold a clip instead and tap Delete in its popup. The bin on each clip, when Pin and delete buttons is on, still deletes it either way. This setting is on by default.

title: Swipe to pin
name: clipboard_swipe_pin_title
description: Which way a swipe pins a clip instead of deleting it
help: By default a swipe in either direction deletes the clip. Pick a direction and the two directions do two things: that way pins or unpins the clip, which slides back into place, and the other way deletes it. Right pins, left deletes, or the other way round.

title: Undo a deleted clip
name: clipboard_undo_delete_title
description: After you delete a clip, show an Undo button for a few seconds
help: A swipe across a card deletes the clip with no question first, and a swipe is easy to make by accident while you scroll. With this setting on, a bar at the bottom of the panel offers the clip back. Delete more clips while the bar is up and one Undo brings them all back, each to the place it had. The bar stays for five seconds, or longer if you have set a longer time to take action in Android's accessibility settings. This setting is on by default.

title: Ask before deleting a pinned clip
name: clipboard_confirm_pinned_delete_title
description: Deleting a pinned clip asks first; unpinned clips go at once
help: You pin a clip to keep it, so losing one to a stray tap on its bin or a swipe made while scrolling costs more than losing any other clip. With this setting on, deleting a pinned clip from the panel shows a question first, and only Delete removes it. Unpinned clips are deleted straight away, as before. This setting is on by default.

title: Search bar
name: clipboard_search_title
description: Show a search bar at the top of the clipboard panel. It filters the history as you type

title: Regular expressions
name: clipboard_search_regex_title
description: Read the search as a pattern, such as ^https or \\d{6}
help: With this setting on, what you type in the clipboard search is a regular expression instead of plain text. ^https finds clips that start with a web address, \\d{6} finds six digits in a row, and invoice|receipt finds either word. Case never matters. A pattern that is not finished yet, like an open bracket, searches as plain text until it is, so the list does not go blank while you type. This setting is off by default.

title: Clear button
name: clipboard_clear_button_title
description: Show a bin beside the search bar that deletes all unpinned clips
help: The bin asks before it deletes. Pinned clips always stay. It also empties the system clipboard, unless that holds a pinned clip. When Undo a deleted clip is on, the Undo bar gives all of the clips back. This setting is off by default.

title: Link previews
name: clipboard_link_previews_title
description: Get the page title of a copied link and show it in the panel. This contacts the linked site

title: Pop-up when you copy
name: clipboard_toast_title
description: Show a short "Copied" pop-up when you copy or cut text from the keyboard
help: This works for the copy actions of the keyboard: the A/C/V/X clipboard shortcuts and the copy button of the text editing panel. It works only for fields that give no copy feedback of their own. This setting is off by default.

title: Maximum entries
name: clipboard_max_title
description: How many unpinned clips the history keeps
help: This is the second limit on the history. The clipboard expiry above is the first one. A busy day of copying can make hundreds of clips well inside the expiry time. When the panel is full, each new copy deletes the oldest unpinned clip. Pinned clips do not count against this limit, and the keyboard never deletes them. Unlimited keeps every clip until the expiry deletes it. With the expiry set to never as well, nothing is deleted, and a very long history makes the panel slower to open.

title: Clipboard expiry
name: clipboard_expiry_title
description: Delete unpinned clips after this time

title: Longest clip kept
name: clipboard_max_chars_title
description: Cut very long copied text to this many characters
help: With no limit, the default, the history keeps all of the text you copy. Set a limit and a longer copy is kept cut to that many characters, so a copied book does not fill the history and your backups. Rich text that gets cut is kept as plain text. The system clipboard itself keeps all of the text, so a normal paste in an app is not changed. Gboard cuts at 20,000 characters.

title: Pinned entries last
name: clipboard_pinned_last_title
description: List pinned clips at the end of the panel instead of the top

title: Keep pinned clips in place
name: clipboard_pinned_in_place_title
description: Pinned clips stay among the others instead of moving to the top or the end
help: A pinned clip keeps its pin, so it never expires, but it stays where it was copied in the history, the way SwiftKey shows pins. With this setting on, Pinned entries last and the Pinned and unpinned tabs have no effect. This setting is off by default.

title: Pinned folders
name: clipboard_pinned_folders_title
description: File tagged pinned clips in a folder for each tag
help: A pinned clip with a tag leaves the pinned clips and goes into a folder named after the tag, so clips you only need together stay out of the way until you open their folder. Give a clip a tag from its press-and-hold popup. A clip with two tags is in both folders. Pinned clips without a tag stay where they are. With Keep pinned clips in place on, the folders sit over the whole history. This setting is off by default.

title: Your screenshots
name: clipboard_screenshots_title
description: Show your screenshots in the clipboard next to copied text and images

title: Show the source app
name: clipboard_track_source_title
description: Record which app a clip comes from. Each clip shows that app's icon, and its name when you press and hold it. This needs the Usage Access permission
help: The keyboard reads the app in the foreground at the moment you copy, through Usage Access. Some copies have no source app, for example a copy from a background sync. Nothing about your app usage leaves your device.

title: Suggest the last copy
name: clipboard_suggest_recent_title
description: Show the last copied text as a chip on the suggestion strip. One press pastes it

title: How long the paste chip stays
name: clipboard_chip_life_title
description: Time before the recently copied chip hides itself
help: The chip appears on the suggestion strip after you copy something, so that you can paste it without opening the clipboard. Typing does not dismiss it, because it is meant to survive writing the message you will paste it into. Set a shorter time if you would rather what you copied stopped being on screen, which matters for a password or an address. You can always dismiss the chip yourself.

title: Recent copies on the strip
name: clipboard_recent_chips_title
description: How many of your latest copies the row of recent copies shows
help: The strip shows one chip for the last copy, for as long as the setting above says. Set more than 1, and the chip gets a clock button that opens a row of that many of your latest text clips, newest first, which you can scroll, each one a press from pasted. The row stays until you type, press its cross, or move to another field. It never opens by itself. The Recent copies tool opens the same row, from the toolbar or from a press and hold you give it, such as the Copy tool's. Hidden clips never appear. The default is 1.

title: Compact paste chip
name: clipboard_compact_paste_chip_title
description: Keep the paste chip narrow, however long the copy
help: A long copy stretches the paste chip across the strip whenever no words are showing, which hides the tools beside it. With this on the chip always keeps its narrow form, about a third of the strip, so the rest of the row stays in reach. Off by default.

title: Suggest copied codes
name: clipboard_suggest_codes_title
description: Offer a copied one-time code as a paste chip
help: A code on its own is treated as a secret, and a secret is normally kept off the suggestion strip, because the chip stays in view while you type. A code you copied by hand is the case that rule was never aimed at: you copied it to paste it, and it is one tap away in the clipboard panel either way. "Any field" offers a code copied in the last few minutes wherever you are typing. "Code boxes only" limits that to fields that ask for digits, so a code never appears over the keys of a message. Either way this covers codes only. A copied password is never offered.

title: Detect codes, numbers and links
name: clipboard_entities_title
description: Take one-time codes, phone numbers and links out of your clips. Each one becomes its own chip
help: The chips sit above the history in dashed outlines, so they read as parts of a clip and not as clips of their own. Press and hold a chip to see it marked inside the clip that it comes from. A press pastes only that part, and the clip stays in the history. The keyboard finds these parts on your device.

title: Show the found parts as icons on each clip
name: clipboard_entity_icons_title
description: In place of the chips above the history
help: Each clip shows a small icon for each kind of part found in it: a link, a phone number or a code. A number on the icon says how many there are. Press an icon to see the parts and pick one. The chips above the history go away while this is on. Press and hold a clip and press Extract to do the same from its menu.

title: Copy picked parts to the clipboard
name: clipboard_entity_to_clipboard_title
description: A picked link, number or code becomes a clip, and is not typed

title: Show the found parts on the suggestion strip
name: clipboard_fragments_on_strip_title
description: After a copy, its codes, numbers and links take the strip as chips
help: When you copy something that has a code, a phone number or a link in it, the suggestion strip shows the whole copy as a chip and then a dashed chip for each part. A press pastes that part, so you do not have to open the clipboard. The chips stay until you type something or press the ✕, and then the strip shows words again with the usual chip for the copy. This setting is off by default.

title: Keep the keyboard's copies private
name: clipboard_private_copies_title
description: Copy and cut from the keyboard stay in the keyboard, and other apps cannot read them
help: Any app can read the system clipboard, so text you copy there can be read by apps you did not mean to give it to. With this setting on, text you copy or cut with the keyboard's own keys, tools and panels never goes to the system clipboard. It goes into the clipboard history instead, and the keyboard's paste keys and the clipboard panel paste it. The copy and paste menu of other apps does not see it. Incognito has its own switch for this, which holds only while incognito is on. This setting is off by default.

title: Forget after you paste a password
name: clipboard_password_paste_title
description: Delete a clip from the history and from the system clipboard as soon as you paste it into a password field
help: Every app on your device can read the system clipboard. Without this setting, a password from a password manager stays readable there until it expires. This applies to the pastes that you make with the keyboard into a password field: the clipboard panel, the paste chip, hold V and Ctrl+V. This setting is off by default.

title: Sensitive clips
name: clipboard_sensitive_title
description: What to do with a copied password or one-time code
help: Android lets an app mark what it puts on the clipboard as sensitive. A password manager does this when you copy a login. Nothing else on your device acts on that mark, so the keyboard acts on it here. A hidden clip shows as dots in the panel. The keyboard never offers it as a paste chip and never puts it in a settings backup. It deletes itself on the short timer below and not on the history expiry. If you pin the clip, none of that applies, because a pin means "keep this". By default the keyboard keeps these clips like any other.

title: Let the keyboard find them
name: clipboard_detect_sensitive_title
description: Also treat a clip that looks like a password or a bare verification code as sensitive, not only the clips that the copying app marks
help: Most password managers are older than the sensitive mark of Android, and a code that you copy by hand out of a message carries no mark at all. The keyboard looks for these clips on your device, and the test is narrow on purpose. A clip matches only when the whole clip is one token: a short run of capital letters and digits, or a long mix of capital letters, small letters, digits and symbols. Sentences, links and email addresses never match.

title: Forget sensitive clips after
name: clipboard_sensitive_expiry_title
description: This time is separate from the history expiry above

title: Template variables
name: expander_variables_title
help: A variable expands at the moment that you insert the snippet, not when you save it. Because of this, {date} always gives the current date. {date:…} takes a pattern, for example {date:EEEE} or {date:dd/MM/yy}.

title: Patterns
name: expander_pattern_title
help: A pattern lets one snippet take a different piece of text each time. Give the snippet the pattern ^hello (.+)$ and the text "Hello, $1! Nice to meet you." Then type "hello John" and a space, and the keyboard writes "Hello, John! Nice to meet you." Use $1 to $9 for each part in brackets, and ${1:upper}, ${1:lower}, ${1:title} or ${1:trim} to change one. One backspace puts back what you typed.

title: When a snippet has several expansions
name: expander_multi_expand_title
description: What happens after you type the trigger
help: A snippet can hold more than one text, and can point at other snippets. Chips only: the suggestion bar offers all of them and nothing goes in until you press one. Insert first: the keyboard inserts the default straight away and offers the rest, so pressing one swaps what it put in. Each snippet can answer this on its own.

title: Panel columns
name: expander_grid_columns_title
description: How many snippet tiles sit side by side in the keyboard's panel
help: More columns show more snippets at once, which suits short labels. Fewer give each tile more room for its text. Folders use the same grid. The default is 2.

title: Names only
name: expander_titles_only_title
description: Show each snippet in the panel by its name alone, without its text, so more fit

title: Stay open after inserting
name: expander_panel_stays_title
description: Keep the snippets panel open when you tap a snippet, to insert several in a row

title: Expand in password fields
name: expander_secure_fields_title
description: Let a trigger you type turn into its snippet inside a password box
help: Off by default. With it on, pressing space or Enter in a password field, or typing the symbol a trigger ends in, makes the keyboard read back the few characters before the cursor and check them against your triggers. Nothing it reads is learned, kept or sent. The space that ends a trigger is not typed into the password; Enter still does what the field asks. Patterns, chips that ask first and apps typing snippets through automation stay off in password fields, and number-only PIN fields are not covered.

title: Escape character
name: expander_escape_title
description: Type it in front of a trigger that expands immediately to keep the trigger as text
help: A snippet set to expand immediately replaces its trigger as soon as you type the last letter. Type this character just before the trigger and the trigger stays as text. The character itself is removed. The default is a backslash, so \\btw gives btw. Choose Off if you use this character in front of words.

title: Import snippets from
name: expander_import_source_title
description: A .yml match file or a package .zip from the Espanso Hub.

title: Export snippets as
name: expander_export_target_title
description: A .yml file to put in Espanso's match folder on a computer.

title: All emoji settings
name: tooldetail_emoji_all_title
description: Suggestions, the history tab, the emoji row, skin tones and favourites

title: All clipboard settings
name: tooldetail_clipboard_all_title
description: History, the panel, the paste chip, and what happens to a copied password

title: All Text Expander settings
name: tooldetail_snippets_all_title
description: Your snippets, triggers, patterns and template variables

title: All layout and size settings
name: tooldetail_layout_nav_title
description: Keyboard height, width, alignment and split

title: All layout and size settings
name: tooldetail_layout_nav_title
description: Keyboard height, width, alignment and floating mode

title: All layout and size settings
name: tooldetail_layout_nav_title
description: Keyboard height, width, alignment and the keep-on-screen switch

title: Turn off with the keyboard
name: tooldetail_flashlight_auto_off_title
description: Turn the torch off when the keyboard closes
help: On: a torch you turned on from the keyboard goes off when the keyboard closes or when you change apps, so it is never left on in your pocket. A torch turned on from the quick settings tile or another app is left alone. Off: the torch stays on until you turn it off again, from the tool or from the quick settings tile of the system.

title: Degree readout
name: tooldetail_compass_degrees_title
description: Show the heading in numbers under the compass rose

title: Show the qibla
name: tooldetail_compass_qibla_title
description: Mark the direction of the Kaaba on the compass
help: The keyboard computes the qibla bearing from the location that you save in the weather tool. The two tools share that location. The keyboard computes everything on your device, and the compass never uses the network.

title: Angle readout
name: tooldetail_level_angles_title
description: Show the pitch and the roll in degrees under the bubble

title: Redo sends Ctrl+Y
name: tooldetail_redo_ctrl_y_title
description: Instead of the default Ctrl+Shift+Z
help: Both shortcuts are standard for redo. Which one works depends on the app that you type in. If redo does nothing, try the other one.

title: Redo sends Ctrl+Y
name: tooldetail_redo_ctrl_y_title
description: Instead of the default Ctrl+Shift+Z
help: Both shortcuts are standard for redo. Which one works depends on the app that you type in. If redo does nothing, try the other one.

title: Southern hemisphere
name: tooldetail_moon_southern_title
description: Show the moon the way it looks south of the equator

title: Arabic names too
name: tooldetail_moon_arabic_title
description: Show the name of each phase in Arabic as well, under the name in your language

title: Fahrenheit
name: tooldetail_weather_fahrenheit_title
description: Show temperatures in °F instead of °C

title: Fetch the forecast as you type
name: tooldetail_weather_auto_fetch_title
description: Off, a weather chip waits for your tap before it goes online
help: This setting controls only the chip on the suggestion strip. The panel fetches the forecast when you open it. The F-Droid edition starts with this setting off.

title: Open the clock
name: clock_open_title
description: Alarms, timers, stopwatch, world clocks, countdowns and history

title: Show seconds
name: clock_show_seconds_title
description: On the big clock and on the clock faces

title: Sort cities by time
name: clock_sort_zones_title
description: List the world clocks with the earliest time first, instead of in the order you added them

title: Cities in a grid
name: clock_zones_grid_title
description: Show the world clocks two to a row, so more fit in the panel

title: Default format
name: clock_insert_format_title
description: A hold on your own clock types this one at once, and a hold on a city offers it first

title: Vibrate
name: clock_vibrate_title
description: While an alarm or a timer rings

title: Fade in
name: clock_fade_title
description: An alarm starts quiet and gets louder over this time. Timers always ring at full volume.

title: Stop ringing after
name: clock_auto_silence_title
description: An alarm nobody answers stops by itself and shows as missed in the history

title: Snooze when nobody answers
name: clock_auto_snooze_title
description: An alarm that stops ringing by itself snoozes instead, up to this many times or until someone answers, before it counts as missed

title: Notice before an alarm
name: clock_upcoming_title
description: Shows the next alarm in the notifications this long before it rings, with a button to skip it

title: Notice while snoozed
name: clock_snoozed_notice_title
description: Shows a snoozed alarm in the notifications, with a button to end the snooze

title: Notice for a missed alarm
name: clock_missed_notice_title
description: Leaves a notification when an alarm rang with nobody to answer it

title: Volume keys snooze
name: clock_volume_keys_title
description: On the ring screen. When off, the volume keys do nothing there.

title: Allow exact alarms
name: clock_grant_exact_title
description: Without it, Android can ring an alarm some minutes late

title: Default format
name: location_format_title
description: What Insert types. Hold a format on the panel to make it the default.

title: Map link
name: location_map_link_title
description: The map that a shared link opens

title: Precision
name: location_precision_title
description: How much of your position a share gives away
help: A coarser precision moves the point to the centre of a fixed square of that size. The square is the same each time, so many shares from one place cannot be averaged back to that place. The address, the link and the Plus code all use the moved point.

title: Look up the address
name: location_lookup_address_title
description: Show a street and a city, not only numbers
help: The keyboard sends the point, at the precision you chose, to the address server one time for each share. The default server is Nominatim from OpenStreetMap. Off, nothing about your position leaves the phone until you send the text yourself.

title: Locate when the tool opens
name: location_locate_on_open_title
description: If Android already allows it. Off, the panel waits for Locate me.

title: Tile server
name: location_tiles_label
description: Map behind the dial

title: Saved places
name: location_places_group
description: Insert a saved place from the Places tab. It needs no location access and no network.

title: Location access
name: location_permission_title
description: Read only when you tap Locate me or Use my location. Never in the background.

title: Song recognisers
name: music_providers_title
description: Who is asked what a clip is, in order, until one names the song. Each needs a key of yours, and each is sent the clip.
help: Who is asked what a clip is, in order, until one names the song. Each needs a key of yours, and each is sent the clip.

title: Insert as
name: music_text_format_title
description: What the Insert button types. Every other shape is a chip beside it.

title: Picture style
name: music_card_style_title
description: The picture the Picture chip makes first. The others are one tap further.

title: Open in
name: music_open_link_title
description: Which store a link points to, when the song is on it

title: Listen for
name: music_clip_seconds_title
description: How long the microphone records before asking. Longer clips match more reliably and cost the same.

title: Check what the phone plays first
name: music_now_playing_first_title
description: Read the song from the player on this phone before listening, where notification access allows it

title: Keep a history
name: music_keep_history_title
description: Remember the songs recognised, on this phone only

title: Recognised songs
name: music_history_open_title
description: Every song the tool has named, newest first

title: Smart home tool
name: ha_enabled_title
description: Lights, switches, climate, media, scenes and sensors as tiles in the keyboard, live

title: Homes
name: smarthome_homes_title
description: Every home on the list is connected while the tool runs, and its rooms join the panel's tabs. Add a Home Assistant, Google Home, SmartThings, a Hue bridge, an openHAB server, a Smart Life (Tuya) project or a SwitchBot account; more than one is fine.
help: Every home on the list is connected while the tool runs, and its rooms join the panel's tabs. Add a Home Assistant, Google Home, SmartThings, a Hue bridge, an openHAB server, a Smart Life (Tuya) project or a SwitchBot account; more than one is fine.

title: Favourites and rooms
name: ha_favourites_title
description: Pick the tiles the Favourites tab shows, and hide what you never use

title: A tab per room
name: ha_areas_tabs_title
description: Your rooms as each home orders them; with several homes, the home's name comes first. Off, there is Favourites and All.

title: Hold to confirm risky actions
name: ha_confirm_risky_title
description: Locks, alarms, garage doors, gates and sirens take a hold instead of a tap

title: Command bar
name: ha_assist_enabled_title
description: Type a sentence for your home at the bottom of the panel

title: Conversation agent
name: ha_assist_agent_title
description: Which of your assistants answers. The list comes from the server once connected.

title: Send the keyboard's language
name: ha_assist_language_title
description: Assist answers in the language you are typing in

title: Stay connected
name: ha_lifetime_title
description: Home Assistant, a Hue bridge and openHAB hold a connection open so tiles change the moment the house does; SmartThings, Smart Life and SwitchBot are asked every few seconds to once a minute instead. It costs little, but it is a connection.
help: Home Assistant, a Hue bridge and openHAB hold a connection open so tiles change the moment the house does; SmartThings, Smart Life and SwitchBot are asked every few seconds to once a minute instead. It costs little, but it is a connection.

title: Keep the last states on the phone
name: ha_cache_title
description: The panel draws your tiles at once from the last session, dimmed until each home confirms them

title: Let the AI chat control your home
name: ha_ai_tools_title
description: The chat's tools include your homes; each one asks before it acts

title: Suggest commands as you type
name: ha_smart_chip_title
description: "turn off the lights" in any field offers a chip that sends it to Assist instead of the words

title: First calendar
name: tooldetail_calendar_first_title
description: Its day number also shows inside each day cell

title: Second calendar
name: tooldetail_calendar_second_title
description: The keyboard shows it in the header and under the selected day

title: Weekend
name: toolai_weekend_title
description: The weekday initials that the month grid tints

title: Hijri day adjustment
name: tooldetail_calendar_hijri_title
description: Move the computed Hijri date to match the local moon sighting
help: The tool uses the arithmetic (tabular) Hijri calendar. Real Islamic months start at the sighting of the crescent moon. That can differ from the tables by one or two days. Set the offset that matches your local authority.

title: Save events
name: tooldetail_calendar_save_mode_title
description: Where Save puts a new event
help: In the keyboard writes the event straight into your calendar, and asks for calendar access the first time. In the calendar app opens your calendar app's own editor with the event filled in, and you save it there. Changing and deleting events always happens in the keyboard.

title: Default calendar
name: tooldetail_calendar_default_calendar_title
description: The calendar a new event starts in

title: Event length
name: tooldetail_calendar_default_length_title
description: How long a new event runs

title: Reminder
name: tooldetail_calendar_default_reminder_title
description: The reminder a new event starts with

title: Start with the selfie camera
name: tooldetail_camera_front_title
description: Open the tool on the front camera instead of the back one

title: Mirror selfies
name: tooldetail_camera_mirror_title
description: Save front camera photos the way the preview shows them
help: Camera sensors record selfies without a mirror. The text then reads correctly, but the photo looks turned around next to the preview. On: the saved photo matches what you saw while you framed it. Off: the keyboard keeps the true orientation of the sensor.

title: Send the whole photo
name: tooldetail_camera_fullframe_title
description: Keep the full 4:3 picture instead of the part in the viewfinder
help: The viewfinder is as wide as the keyboard, so the top and the bottom of the picture go off the screen. The keyboard usually cuts those parts away, and you send what you saw. On: you send the full 4:3 photo, which holds more than the viewfinder showed you. The preview does not change.

title: Save to the gallery
name: tooldetail_camera_gallery_title
description: Also keep photos in Pictures/WM Keyboard
help: This setting is off by default, because photos that you take here are normally one-time sends and not photos to keep. On: the keyboard copies every photo into the gallery and also sends it.

title: Search button
name: tooldetail_camera_search_button_title
description: Add Search next to Retake and Send

title: Stamp the place on photos
name: location_camera_stamp_title
description: A band along the bottom with the address, coordinates, time and Plus code. The pin on the viewfinder turns this on and off.

title: Add the place as text
name: location_camera_caption_title
description: Send puts the place in the text box too, in the location tool's default format
help: The text goes in first, then the photo. Many chat apps use the text in the box as the photo's caption; others send it as a message of its own.

title: Search with
name: tooldetail_camera_search_with_title
help: Google Lens and the share sheet give the photo to another app, and the keyboard sends nothing itself. Web sends the photo to the search site that you pick and opens the results in your browser.

title: Search site
name: tooldetail_camera_search_engine_title
help: None of these sites has a public way to send photos. The keyboard does what the site's own upload button does, so a site can stop working when it changes. If that happens, pick a different site. Custom sends the photo to your own server.

title: Shutter sound
name: tooldetail_camera_shutter_title
description: Play the camera click when you take a photo

title: Look up the word at the cursor
name: tooldetail_dictionary_auto_title
description: The tool searches the selected word or the current word when it opens

title: Dictionary sources
name: tooldetail_dictionary_sources_title
description: Where the tool looks for definitions, in order
help: The tool asks the first source that is on. When that source does not know the word, or cannot be reached, the tool asks the next one. Drag a source to change the order, and turn off a source to never ask it. Online sources receive only the word you look up.

title: Show translations
name: tooldetail_dictionary_translations_title
description: Show the word in other languages under its definitions. Tap a translation to type it
help: Translations come from Wiktionary. When the word was found in Wiktionary, its translations come on the same page, so nothing more is sent. When another source found the word, the tool asks Wiktionary for the translations as well, but only if Wiktionary is on in the dictionary sources.

title: Vocabulary packs
name: tooldetail_vocab_packs_title
description: Download a word list to start

title: My lists
name: tooldetail_vocab_lists_title
description: Lists you make yourself

title: Review
name: tooldetail_vocab_review_title
description: Flashcards for what is due today

title: Browse words
name: tooldetail_vocab_browse_title
description: Every word in your packs

title: Offer stronger words
name: tooldetail_vocab_nudges_title
description: A chip when a plainer word could be one from your packs
help: When you type a plain word that a pack has a stronger alternative for, a chip on the suggestion strip offers it: “hate → abhor”. Tap it for the word’s card, hold it to swap the word.

title: Also for the words themselves
name: tooldetail_vocab_nudge_self_title
description: Typing a pack word offers its card

title: Tapping the chip
name: tooldetail_vocab_tap_title
description: Holding it does the other

title: Sensitivity
name: tooldetail_vocab_level_title
description: How much plainer the typed word has to be

title: Tapping a synonym or antonym
name: tooldetail_vocab_related_title
description: Holding one always types it

title: Translation languages
name: tooldetail_vocab_translations_title
description: Your keyboard languages

title: Providers
name: providers_group_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The services this tool asks, in order. Drag a provider to move it, switch one off to skip it, or add your own server. Some providers can be added twice, with a second key or account. A provider that cannot be reached is skipped for a minute, so the next one answers at once.

title: Accent
name: tooldetail_vocab_accent_title
description: The pronunciation shown and spoken

title: New words a day
name: tooldetail_vocab_goal_title
description: Added to a review session on top of what is due

title: Card on the home screen
name: tooldetail_vocab_wotd_card_title
description: One word a day, drawn from your packs

title: Chip on the keyboard
name: tooldetail_vocab_wotd_chip_title
description: Offered on the suggestion strip until you tap or dismiss it

title: A new word every
name: tooldetail_vocab_wotd_interval_title
description: The same word for everyone with your packs, in that span

title: Times the chip comes back
name: tooldetail_vocab_wotd_chip_times_title
description: How many text fields may offer the same word before it stops; dismissing it stops it at once

title: Key repeat interval
name: tooldetail_text_edit_repeat_title
description: Pause between repeats while you hold an arrow or backspace. A lower value is faster

title: Panel layout
name: panel_layout_row_title
description: Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel

title: Horizontal sensitivity
name: tooldetail_trackpad_step_x_title
description: How far your finger travels for each character. A lower value moves the cursor faster

title: Vertical sensitivity
name: tooldetail_trackpad_step_y_title
description: How far your finger travels for each line. A lower value moves the cursor faster

title: Press and hold to open
name: tooldetail_trackpad_hold_title
description: The trackpad stays open while you hold the tool and closes when you let go. A tap opens it until the next tap
help: This spends the press and hold on the toolbar, so this page is where you change the tool, or a hold in the toolbox. To move the tool, press and hold it and then drag it, as before.

title: Two taps select a word
name: tooldetail_trackpad_taps_title
description: Two quick taps on the trackpad select the word at the cursor. Three select the full line

title: Vibrate on each move
name: tooldetail_trackpad_haptics_title
description: A short tick for every character or line the cursor moves

title: Show the trail
name: tooldetail_trackpad_trail_title
description: Draw your finger's path and a crosshair on the trackpad while you drag

title: Magnifier
name: tooldetail_trackpad_magnifier_title
description: Show the text at the cursor, larger, above the cursor while you drag
help: The magnifier shows the line of text around the cursor. It goes above the cursor when the app tells the keyboard where the cursor is. If the app does not, it goes above the keyboard.

title: Hold to repeat on the toolbar
name: tooldetail_cursor_repeat_title
description: Holding this tool on the toolbar keeps moving the cursor. Off, holding it opens this page instead
help: One switch for all eight moving cursor tools. Dragging the tool from the toolbar still moves it.

title: Hold to repeat in the toolbox
name: tooldetail_cursor_repeat_toolbox_title
description: Do the same in the toolbox grid. This tool only, and off by default
help: A hold in the toolbox is how you open a tool's page from the keyboard, so this tool gives that up while this is on. Its page stays under Tools. Turn it on only for the moves you actually hold.

title: Word steps
name: tooldetail_word_steps_title
description: Where Word left and Word right stop, and what Select word takes
help:
The same setting applies to Word left, Word right and Select word.

Press Select word again to also select the word on each side. Press shift and then Select word to go back one step. If "Shift changes the case of the selection" is on, shift changes the case instead.

title: Stop at capitals
name: tooldetail_word_steps_capitals_title
description: "GrapheneOS" is two words: "Graphene" and "OS"

title: Stop at numbers
name: tooldetail_word_steps_digits_title
description: "word1" is two words: "word" and "1"

title: Press and hold to select
name: tooldetail_select_mode_hold_title
description: Selection mode stays on while you hold the tool. It stops when you let go, and the selected text stays selected
help: This spends the press and hold on the toolbar, so this page is where you change the tool, or a hold in the toolbox. To move the tool, press and hold it and then drag it, as before.

title: Two presses select a word
name: tooldetail_select_mode_taps_title
description: Two quick presses select the word at the cursor. Three select the full line
help: The first press of a pair still turns selection mode on or off, in the same way the shift key gives you caps lock. Turn this off if you press the tool twice in quick succession and want no word selected.

title: Calculator layout
name: tooldetail_numpad_calc_title
description: 7 8 9 on the top row, like a desk keypad. Off puts 1 2 3 on top, like a dialer

title: Remember searches
name: tooldetail_find_history_title
description: Offer your last ten searches when the Find field is empty. Never kept in incognito or from a password field

title: Save to notes from other apps
name: tooldetail_notes_share_title
description: An entry in the share sheet

title: Format Markdown
name: tooldetail_notes_markdown_title
description: Show headings, lists and checklists formatted in the keyboard and in previews. Off, every note is plain text.

title: The keyboard panel opens on
name: tooldetail_notes_panel_start_title
description: What you see when you tap the tool

title: Keyboard panel layout
name: tooldetail_notes_panel_layout_title
description: How the list of notes is laid out in the keyboard

title: Save as note from a selection
name: tooldetail_notes_save_selection_title
description: What the selection bar's Save as note does

title: Delete all notes
name: tooldetail_notes_clear_title
description: Every note, every tag and the trash

title: Hide finished tasks in the keyboard
name: tooldetail_todo_hide_done_title
description: The keyboard's list opens with ticked tasks left out. Its Hide done chip shows them again for that visit.

title: Sync with a task app
name: tooldetail_todo_sync_title
description: Keep the list the same as a task list in OpenTasks or Tasks.org. DAVx5 syncs that list with your CalDAV server.
help:
WM Keyboard reads and writes the list through the task app on this phone. It never connects to your server itself; DAVx5 does that, on its own schedule.

Tasks you add here appear in the task app, and tasks you add there appear here. Ticks, edits and deletes go both ways. Steps stay steps. The to-do list has no reminders, so a reminder set in the task app stays there.

jtx Board is not supported. Its provider only answers sync adapters, and a change written that way never reaches the server.

title: Import from the Todo List plugin
name: tooldetail_todo_import_title
description: Copy the plugin's tasks, ticks and due dates into this list. The plugin keeps its own copy and its reminders.

title: Delete all tasks
name: tooldetail_todo_clear_title
description: Every task and step on this phone. With sync on, the task app keeps its own tasks, and the next sync brings them back.

title: Pause learning
name: tooldetail_incognito_learning_title
description: The keyboard learns no words and no emoji habits from your typing

title: Pause clipboard capture
name: tooldetail_incognito_clipboard_title
description: Copies do not go into the history of the clipboard tool

title: Keep copies in the keyboard
name: tooldetail_incognito_private_clipboard_title
description: Copy and cut from the keyboard do not go to the system clipboard, so other apps cannot read them
help:
While incognito is on, text you copy or cut with the keyboard stays inside the keyboard. The paste keys of the keyboard paste it back. When incognito goes off, the keyboard forgets it.

If you have not copied with the keyboard yet, paste gives what is on the system clipboard, as usual. The copy and paste menu of the app itself still uses the system clipboard.

title: Power saving now
name: tooldetail_power_now_title
description: The same switch that the toolbar tool uses
help:
This drops the features below until you turn it off again. It stays on after a restart and at any battery level. A full battery does not turn it off.

Nothing is lost. The features come back exactly as you had them, because power saving never rewrites your settings. It only hides them while it is on.

title: What to drop
name: tooldetail_power_preset_title
description: A bundle of the switches further down

title: Turn on by itself
name: tooldetail_power_trigger_title
description: As well as the switch above
help: "Android battery saver" follows the system switch, so the keyboard saves power exactly when you already asked your device to. "Battery is low" uses your own percentage below instead.

title: Low battery is
name: tooldetail_power_battery_title
description: Power saving starts at this level or below it

title: Off while charging
name: tooldetail_power_charging_title
description: Ignore the automatic triggers while the charger is in
help: There is nothing to save while the battery fills, so the automatic triggers stop. This does not change the switch above. If you turn power saving on by hand, it stays on.

title: Key vibration
name: tooldetail_power_drop_haptics_title
description: Stop the vibration motor

title: Key sounds
name: tooldetail_power_drop_sound_title
description: Stop the key click

title: Glass blur
name: tooldetail_power_drop_glass_blur_title
description: Stop glass themes blurring the app behind the keyboard and its popups

title: Glide typing
name: tooldetail_power_drop_glide_title
description: Turn glide typing off
help: A swipe decode is the most expensive thing the keyboard does. It is also why many people use the keyboard, so this setting is off by default and only the trail is dropped.

title: Emoji suggestions
name: tooldetail_power_drop_emoji_title
description: Stop reading what you type for emoji to offer

title: Animations
name: tooldetail_power_drop_anim_title
description: Stop transitions and motion, as reduced motion does

title: Glide trail
name: tooldetail_power_drop_trail_title
description: Stop drawing the trail behind a swiped word
help: This drops only the trail. Glide typing still works. The keyboard draws the trail on every frame of a gesture, so it costs more than the decode that it decorates.

title: Smart chips
name: tooldetail_power_drop_chips_title
description: Stop matching sums, conversions and tool keywords as you type

title: Background network
name: tooldetail_power_drop_network_title
description: No link previews and no automatic look-ups
help: This stops the requests that happen without you asking: previews for copied links and for scanned QR codes, and the look-up of the dictionary when you select a word. Tools that you open yourself still work, such as translate, search and GIFs.

title: Screenshot watching
name: tooldetail_power_drop_screenshot_title
description: Stop watching for new screenshots to offer in the clipboard

title: On-device models
name: tooldetail_power_drop_models_title
description: Use the system recognizer for voice typing, and glide a word instead of writing it
help: Offline voice typing and handwriting both run a neural model on the processor, which is the most expensive work the keyboard does. Voice typing goes back to the system recognizer, and the letter swipe goes back to glide typing.

title: Media tool pin
name: tooldetail_power_drop_media_pin_title
description: Stop putting the media tool on the toolbar while music plays

title: Pin while music plays
name: tooldetail_mediactl_pin_title
description: Put the media tool on the toolbar on its own while a music app is playing
help: The pin is temporary. It goes on the end of the toolbar, it never moves the tools you pinned yourself, and it disappears when the player does. If you have already pinned the media tool, nothing changes.

title: Music players
name: tooldetail_mediactl_apps_title
description: Which apps count as music. %1$d chosen

title: Use KDE Connect
name: kdeconnect_enabled_title
description: Look for paired computers and let them find this phone

title: Stay connected
name: kdeconnect_lifetime_title
description: While the keyboard is on screen, and for a minute after.
help: There is no background service. The link lives inside the keyboard, so after the keyboard hides it lasts only until Android pauses or closes the keyboard in the background. Many phones do that within minutes, some at once. Setting WM Keyboard's battery use to Unrestricted in Android's app settings keeps it up longer, but nothing guarantees it.

title: Connect automatically
name: kdeconnect_auto_connect_title
description: Reconnect to paired computers when they are found

title: Receive the computer's clipboard
name: kdeconnect_clipboard_receive_title
description: Text copied there is ready to paste here

title: Clear received passwords
name: kdeconnect_clear_secrets_title
description: A password or code copied on the computer leaves this phone's clipboard after this long
help: Only text that looks like a password or a one-time code counts, the same check clipboard history uses. It is cleared only if it is still on the clipboard, and its copy in clipboard history goes too unless pinned. Other text from the computer stays.

title: Send this phone's clipboard
name: kdeconnect_clipboard_send_title
description: Text copied here is ready to paste there
help: Passwords and codes are never sent by themselves. Nothing is sent from a password field, or while incognito pauses the clipboard. The Send tab can still send the clipboard when you ask.

title: Let the computer type here
name: kdeconnect_remote_typing_title
description: Its keyboard types into the field, while this keyboard is showing and the phone is unlocked

title: Use the keyboard language
name: kdeconnect_pipeline_title
description: Run its keys through this keyboard's layout, like a hardware keyboard
help: Off: what the computer sends is typed exactly. On: a Latin keyboard on the desk writes Bengali through Avro, and suggestions and autocorrect apply.

title: Acceleration
name: kdeconnect_pad_accel_title
description: Slow moves are precise, fast moves go far

title: Natural scrolling
name: kdeconnect_natural_scroll_title
description: The page follows your fingers

title: Tap to click
name: kdeconnect_tap_click_title
description: Two fingers for right click, three for middle

title: Receive files
name: kdeconnect_receive_files_title
description: Saved to Downloads, in WM Keyboard, and added to the clipboard history

title: Show in the share menu
name: kdeconnect_share_sheet_title
description: Other apps can share to the computer. Only shown once a computer is paired

title: Report battery level
name: kdeconnect_battery_title
description: The computer shows this phone's charge

title: Send one-time codes
name: kdeconnect_codes_title
description: A verification code that arrives here is offered on the computer too
help: When a code arrives in a notification, the phone sends the code alone to the paired computer, never the message it came in. WM Keyboard on the computer offers it above the cursor, and a KDE Connect desktop shows it as a notification. Everything stays on your local network. This needs Codes from notifications on, under Typing, because that is what reads the notifications.

title: Offer this phone's media
name: kdeconnect_media_title
description: The computer can pause and skip what plays here

title: Open apps
name: tooldetail_launcher_open_mode_title
description: What a tap on an app does
help: A press and hold on an app offers all three whatever you pick here. Split screen puts the app beside the one you are typing in and needs Android 12L or later. A floating window needs a device with a desktop or freeform window mode, such as many tablets; elsewhere the app opens full screen.

title: Sort order
name: tooldetail_launcher_sort_title
description: How the app grid orders the apps

title: App names
name: tooldetail_launcher_labels_title
description: Show each app's name under its icon

title: Apps per row
name: tooldetail_launcher_columns_title
description: How many apps sit side by side in the grid
help: Auto fits as many apps as the keyboard width holds, three to six on most phones. Set a number to get larger targets or more apps on the screen. If the icons do not fit in a row, they become smaller.

title: Icon size
name: tooldetail_launcher_icon_size_title
description: How large each app icon is in the grid
help: With apps per row on Auto, larger icons also make each cell wider, so fewer apps fit in a row. The pinned and recent row keeps its own size.

title: Icon shape
name: tooldetail_launcher_icon_shape_title
description: The outline of each app icon
help: As on the phone shows each icon with the shape your home screen gives it. Old apps without an adaptive icon keep their own outline.

title: Work apps
name: tooldetail_launcher_work_title
description: Also list the apps in your work profile
help: Work apps carry a briefcase on their icon. While work apps are paused they show dimmed, and opening one asks Android to turn work apps back on. The keyboard needs no extra permission for this.

title: Recent apps
name: tooldetail_launcher_recents_title
description: Show the apps you opened last in a row above the grid
help: The keyboard keeps the last 10 apps you opened from this tool, on your device only. Turn this off to stop the tracking and delete the list.

title: Open screens inside apps
name: tooldetail_launcher_drilldown_title
description: List an app’s screens on its page
help: Press and hold an app and pick the last item in the menu to open its page. With this off the page keeps its pin, hide and App info actions and leaves the screens out.

title: Show private screens
name: tooldetail_launcher_non_exported_title
description: Also list screens that only the app itself may open
help: Android does not let other apps open these screens. They show dimmed, and a press on one does nothing. Useful to explore what an app contains.

title: All typing settings
name: tooldetail_typing_nav_title
description: Suggestions, autocorrect, capital letters and more

title: All selection action settings
name: tooldetail_selection_actions_nav_title
description: Where the bar appears, which actions it offers, and their order

title: All key press settings
name: tooldetail_keypress_nav_title
description: Haptic style and strength, key preview, press and hold

title: Style to start with
name: tooldetail_fancy_style_title
description: The style the tool turns on. The strip over the keys still changes it
help: Select a style and the tool always starts there. The strip over the keys changes the style for the rest of the session, and your selection here stays as it is.

title: Keep the language after you turn it off
name: tooldetail_fancy_keep_title
description: Fancy text stays in the language cycle of the 🌐 key
help: The tool adds Fancy text to your languages when you turn it on. With this setting off, the tool deletes it again when you turn it off, so the 🌐 key cycles only the languages you read.

title: Turn off when the keyboard closes
name: tooldetail_fancy_auto_off_title
description: The next time you type, the keyboard is back in your own language
help: Fancy text is usually one name or one message. This setting takes the keyboard back to the language you came from as soon as you leave the field. It applies only when the tool turned Fancy text on.

title: Fancy text language
name: tooldetail_fancy_language_nav_title
description: The saved style, and the layout switch

title: Layout to show
name: tooldetail_custom_layout_layout_title
description: The secondary layout the tool puts on screen, or a list to select from
help: With no layout selected here, the tool opens a list of all your secondary layouts, or the only one you have. Select a layout and the tool shows that one directly. A press while a secondary layout is on screen always takes it off again. A key on any layout can also open a secondary layout.

title: Key layouts
name: tooldetail_custom_layout_keymaps_nav_title
description: Make and edit secondary layouts

title: Stylus only
name: tooldetail_handwriting_stylus_title
description: Only an S Pen or another stylus draws. The keyboard ignores finger touches
help: This helps to reject the palm while you write with a stylus. Even with this setting off, the keyboard ignores finger touches for a short time after stylus strokes, so a resting palm does not draw.

title: Automatic space
name: tooldetail_handwriting_auto_space_title
description: Put a space between words that you write one after another

title: Offline recogniser for Chinese and Japanese
name: tooldetail_handwriting_zinnia_title
description: Read Chinese and Japanese with zinnia instead of Google ML Kit
help: zinnia is a small open-source recogniser with models from the Tegaki project. It reads one character at a time and is less accurate than ML Kit, but needs nothing from Google. Builds without ML Kit, such as the F-Droid one, always use it. Simplified or Traditional Chinese follows the Traditional characters switch in Chinese settings.

title: Recognition pause
name: tooldetail_handwriting_pause_title
description: How long after the last stroke the keyboard waits before it recognizes the word
help: A shorter pause feels faster, but it can cut multi-stroke letters and Bengali conjuncts in half. A longer pause gives you more time between strokes. Gboard uses about half a second.

title: Panel layout
name: panel_layout_row_title
description: Arrange the keys and the parts of this panel

title: Full-screen writing
name: tooldetail_handwriting_full_screen_title
description: How the full-screen canvas tells your writing apart from taps on the app
help: Tap the expand button on the handwriting panel to write anywhere over the app. The keyboard shrinks to a small bar and the canvas is see-through, so you can watch the text arrive.

title: Languages and layouts
name: tooldetail_handwriting_languages_title
description: Add a language to get its handwriting model here

title: All theme settings
name: tooldetail_themes_nav_title
description: Create, edit, import and export keyboard themes

title: Icon packs
name: tooldetail_appearance_icons_nav_title
description: Install and choose the icons on the keys and tools

title: Emoji font
name: tooldetail_appearance_emoji_nav_title
description: Choose which set the keyboard draws emoji with

title: Key fonts
name: tooldetail_appearance_fonts_nav_title
description: Choose the font the keys are lettered in

title: All layout and size settings
name: tooldetail_layout_nav_title
description: Keyboard height, width, alignment and one-handed mode

title: Providers
name: providers_group_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The services this tool asks, in order. Drag a provider to move it, switch one off to skip it, or add your own server. Some providers can be added twice, with a second key or account. A provider that cannot be reached is skipped for a minute, so the next one answers at once.

title: DeepL Write
name: tooldetail_deepl_write_title
description: Adds a DeepL Write button to the grammar panel and a DeepL Write action to the selection actions
help: DeepL Write corrects and rewrites text in the same language. It works with a DeepL API Pro key only. A Free key gets an error.

title: Sticker packs
name: tooldetail_sticker_packs_title
description: Make, edit, import and export your own packs

title: Offer your stickers as you type
name: tooldetail_sticker_suggest_title
description: In a chat, type the title of a sticker, one of its keywords or one of its emoji to see it
help: Only your own stickers, from your sticker packs. A sticker shows when the text before the cursor ends with its full title, with one of its keywords, or with one of its emoji. Set the title and the keywords when you edit a sticker in its pack. The keyboard does this only in fields that can receive images, so it never offers a sticker that the app cannot take. It also works in the emoji panel: pick an emoji that one of your stickers has and the sticker shows above the panel. Nothing leaves the phone to find them.

title: Hold to see them bigger
name: tooldetail_sticker_suggest_magnify_title
description: Hold a sticker in the tray to see it large, and slide to see the others

title: Full-screen picker
name: tooldetail_media_full_bleed_title
description: Hide the toolbar and move the search up next to a back button
help: The GIF and sticker panels take the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and the search box moves into the row that they leave. The grid then gets every pixel. This applies to both tools.

title: Full-screen picker
name: tooldetail_media_full_bleed_title
description: Hide the toolbar and move the search up next to a back button
help: The GIF and sticker panels take the whole keyboard. The toolbar, the emoji row and the symbol row step aside, and the search box moves into the row that they leave. The grid then gets every pixel. This applies to both tools.

title: GIFs per row
name: tooldetail_media_gif_per_row_title
description: The most GIFs side by side. Fewer makes each one bigger

title: Stickers per row
name: tooldetail_media_sticker_per_row_title
description: The most stickers side by side. Fewer makes each one bigger

title: Gap between cells
name: tooldetail_media_spacing_title
description: The space around each GIF and sticker in the grid. This applies to both tools

title: Gap between cells
name: tooldetail_media_spacing_title
description: The space around each GIF and sticker in the grid. This applies to both tools

title: Panel height
name: langemoji_panel_height_title
description: How much taller than the keyboard the emoji, GIF and sticker panels open
help: A taller panel shows more emoji, GIFs and stickers at one time. The letters keep their own height, and the three panels have the same height, so the keyboard does not move when you go from one to the next. The panel never covers more than most of the screen, so on a short screen, or with the phone sideways, it can stay shorter than this.

title: Panel height
name: langemoji_panel_height_title
description: How much taller than the keyboard the emoji, GIF and sticker panels open
help: A taller panel shows more emoji, GIFs and stickers at one time. The letters keep their own height, and the three panels have the same height, so the keyboard does not move when you go from one to the next. The panel never covers more than most of the screen, so on a short screen, or with the phone sideways, it can stay shorter than this.

title: Hide the search when you scroll
name: tooldetail_media_hide_header_title
description: Scroll down to fold the search box and the chips away, and scroll up to bring them back
help: The results get the room that the search box, the source chips and the category chips take. When you are at the top of the results, pull down to bring them back. While you type a search, the search box always shows. This applies to both tools.

title: Hide the search when you scroll
name: tooldetail_media_hide_header_title
description: Scroll down to fold the search box and the chips away, and scroll up to bring them back
help: The results get the room that the search box, the source chips and the category chips take. When you are at the top of the results, pull down to bring them back. While you type a search, the search box always shows. This applies to both tools.

title: Remember the last search
name: tooldetail_media_remember_search_title
description: Open the panel on the search you left it on, instead of trending
help: On, closing the panel or moving to another text box keeps the search and the category chip you picked, and the panel opens on them next time. Off, the panel always opens on trending with no search typed. This applies to both tools.

title: Remember the last search
name: tooldetail_media_remember_search_title
description: Open the panel on the search you left it on, instead of trending
help: On, closing the panel or moving to another text box keeps the search and the category chip you picked, and the panel opens on them next time. Off, the panel always opens on trending with no search typed. This applies to both tools.

title: Recent GIFs
name: tooldetail_gif_recent_title
description: Show a Recent chip with the GIFs you sent last
help: The list keeps the last 48 GIFs and stays on the phone. Incognito does not add to it. Turn this off to delete the list.

title: Keep favourites on the phone
name: tooldetail_gif_favourites_offline_title
description: Save a copy of each favourite, so it shows and sends without a connection
help: The copies download when you add a favourite or open Favourites, and only on a connection that data saving allows. Turn this off to delete the copies. Your favourites stay.

title: Providers
name: providers_group_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The services this tool asks, in order. Drag a provider to move it, switch one off to skip it, or add your own server. Some providers can be added twice, with a second key or account. A provider that cannot be reached is skipped for a minute, so the next one answers at once.

title: Providers
name: providers_group_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The services this tool asks, in order. Drag a provider to move it, switch one off to skip it, or add your own server. Some providers can be added twice, with a second key or account. A provider that cannot be reached is skipped for a minute, so the next one answers at once.

title: Send stickers as
name: tooldetail_media_sticker_send_title
description: What the sticker tool gives to the chat app
help: Android has no sticker mark. The only signal is the MIME type of the file, and the receiving app decides. Sticker: the keyboard offers the WhatsApp sticker type first, so stickers arrive as real stickers there. Apps that do not support it get a normal image. Image: the keyboard always sends a plain image.

title: Send GIFs as
name: tooldetail_media_gif_send_title
description: Images by default, because most chat apps animate them
help: Sticker mode works only for GIFs that the source gives in WebP form. Android ships no encoder for animated WebP, so the keyboard cannot turn a real animated GIF into a sticker. Those GIFs always go out as images.

title: Results for each search
name: tooldetail_media_limit_title
description: How many items one search or the trending view loads. Your own sticker packs always show fully.

title: Results for each search
name: tooldetail_media_limit_title
description: How many items one search or the trending view loads. Your own sticker packs always show fully.

title: Providers
name: providers_group_title
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone
help: The services this tool asks, in order. Drag a provider to move it, switch one off to skip it, or add your own server. Some providers can be added twice, with a second key or account. A provider that cannot be reached is skipped for a minute, so the next one answers at once.

title: SafeSearch
name: tooldetail_search_safe_title
description: Filter explicit results

title: Results for each search
name: tooldetail_search_count_title
description: Each search uses one API request either way

title: Show the answer from the search engine
name: tooldetail_search_answer_title
description: A short answer above the results, when the engine writes one
help: Tavily writes a short answer to your query from the pages it found, and some SearXNG instances give instant answers. With this on, that answer shows in a box above the results, with buttons to copy it or put it in your text. Brave gives no answer with a normal search key, so nothing shows when Brave does the search. On Tavily the answer costs no extra credits.

title: Tap a result
name: tooldetail_search_open_browser_title
description: What a tap on a result does. Press and hold one for the menu

title: Images per row
name: tooldetail_image_columns_title
description: How many images sit side by side on the Images tab
help: Fewer columns means larger previews, which is easier to judge before you send one. More columns fits more results without scrolling. GIF results are not affected: they are laid out in justified rows so each one keeps its own shape. This setting is 3 by default.

title: Search depth
name: tooldetail_tavily_advanced_title
description: Faster answers, or better results for more credits
help: Tavily has four search depths. Basic is the default. Ultra fast and Fast answer sooner and cost 1 credit, but they do not take SafeSearch, so results are not filtered at those depths. Advanced looks deeper into each page for the parts that match your query, and costs 2 credits. The free plan gives 1,000 credits each month.

title: Search categories
name: tooldetail_searx_categories_title
description: Show these beside All and Images in the search panel
help: SearXNG sorts its search engines into categories, such as news, videos, science and music. The ones you pick here show as chips in the search panel, beside All and Images, and a tap on one searches in that category only. The list comes from your instance, so it shows only the categories that the instance has. Images is always a tab of its own. The chips show only while a SearXNG instance does the search.

title: Start with everything selected
name: tooldetail_ocr_select_all_title
description: Deselect words to cut the capture down. Off starts empty, and you select the words one by one

title: Text recognition
name: tooldetail_ocr_engine_title
help: ML Kit reads Latin script text, for example English or French, and on a phone with Google Play services also Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Devanagari. Tesseract reads more than 100 languages in most scripts, for example Bangla, Arabic, Russian and Chinese, but each language needs a one-time download. Automatic reads with ML Kit what it can, Chinese and Japanese with PaddleOCR where ML Kit cannot, and every other script with Tesseract.

title: Read codes with zxing-cpp
name: tooldetail_qr_scan_zxing_title
description: Use the open-source reader instead of ML Kit. It is a separate download of about 1 MB
help: Decoding runs on your device with zxing-cpp, without Google services. It works offline and uploads nothing. It reads QR codes, Data Matrix, Aztec, PDF417 and the product and industrial barcodes, such as EAN, UPC and Code 128. Insert types the text of the code at the cursor. A link also gets an Open button.

title: Insert automatically
name: tooldetail_qr_scan_auto_title
description: Type the text of the code as soon as the keyboard finds one, with no confirm press

title: Vibrate on detection
name: tooldetail_qr_scan_haptics_title
description: A short buzz when the keyboard finds a code

title: Load link details
name: tooldetail_qr_scan_preview_title
description: When a code is a web link, get the page title and description and show them above it. This needs an internet connection

title: Use the built-in scanner
name: tooldetail_doc_scan_builtin_title
description: Scan with the keyboard's own scanner instead of Google's
help: This opens the keyboard's own document scanner. It finds the page in the camera picture or a photo, lets you move its corners, flattens it, and can clean it up to white paper in colour, grey or black and white. Scanned pages come back as images. The keyboard puts them into the chat like a camera photo when it opens again. Everything runs on your device, without Google Play services.

title: Save to the gallery
name: tooldetail_doc_scan_gallery_title
description: Also keep scanned pages in Pictures/WM Keyboard

title: All voice typing settings
name: tooldetail_voice_all_title
description: The recognition engine, the microphone view, spoken punctuation and the offline models

title: Checkers
name: tooldetail_grammar_providers_group
description: A service, your own server, or files on the phone

title: English dialect
name: tooldetail_grammar_dialect_title
description: The spelling and style rules to check against

title: Re-check delay
name: tooldetail_grammar_debounce_title
description: Pause after you stop typing before the issues refresh. A lower value feels faster, a higher value does less work

title: Use Harper everywhere
name: tooldetail_grammar_system_title
description: Set WM Keyboard as the spell checker of Android

title: Correctness issues
name: tooldetail_grammar_correctness_title
description: Show or hide this kind of issue in the grammar panel
help: Plain mistakes: a misspelling, a verb that disagrees with its subject, a missing comma, a word swapped for one that sounds like it. Leave these on unless something here is noisy for the way you write.

title: Clarity issues
name: tooldetail_grammar_clarity_title
description: Show or hide this kind of issue in the grammar panel
help: Writing that is correct but harder work to read than it needs to be: long sentences, a word repeated, a phrase that says the same thing twice.

title: Engagement issues
name: tooldetail_grammar_engagement_title
description: Show or hide this kind of issue in the grammar panel
help: Suggestions rather than fixes, offering a stronger way to say the same thing. Turn the group off if you would rather only hear about mistakes.

title: Delivery issues
name: tooldetail_grammar_delivery_title
description: Show or hide this kind of issue in the grammar panel
help: How the writing reads for its audience: spacing and formatting, a form that is standard in one region but not another, an informal turn of phrase.

title: Underline only, no fix popup
name: tooldetail_grammar_no_suggestions_title
description: Mark the spelling mistakes but offer no corrections

title: Wikipedia language
name: tooldetail_wiki_language_label
description: Subdomain code: en, bn, de, fr, es …

title: Markdown links
name: tooldetail_wiki_markdown_title
